Saint Bibiana Virgin and Martyr
(† 363)

.

Patronage: parish, epilepsy, epileptics, hangovers, headaches, insanity, mental illness, mentally ill people, single laywomen, torture victims

.

Saint Bibiana was a native of Rome, born in the fourth century, the daughter and sister of martyrs. Flavian, her Christian father, was apprehended during the reign of Julian the Apostate, branded on the face as a slave, and banished to Toscany, where he died of his wounds a few days later. Her mother, Dafrosa, was beheaded two weeks later. Their two daughters, Bibiana and Demetria, after the death of their parents were stripped of all they had in the world, and then imprisoned with orders to give them no food. The Roman praetorian offered them rewards if they would abandon their faith, and threatened a cruel death if they would not conform, but they replied courageously that the goods and advantages of this world had no attraction for them, and that they would endure a thousand deaths rather than betray their faith and their Saviour. Demetria, after having pronounced this ardent defense, fell to the ground and expired at her sister's side; she is inscribed in the Roman martyrology on June 21st.

.

The officer gave orders that Bibiana be placed in the custody of a woman named Rufina, who was commanded to corrupt her or mistreat her. But the martyr made prayer her shield and remained invincible. Enraged at the courage and perseverance of the young virgin, the persecutor ordered her to be tied to a pillar and whipped until she expired, with scourges tipped with leaden plummets. The Saint underwent this punishment cheerfully, and died at the hands of the executioners. She was buried by a holy priest at a site where afterwards a chapel and then a church were built above her tomb. In 1628 the church was splendidly rebuilt by Pope Urban VIII, and in it he placed the relics of the two sisters and of Saint Dafrosa, their mother.

.

Reflection: Pray for fidelity and patience like Bibiana's under all trials, that neither convenience nor any worldly advantage may ever prevail upon you to transgress the laws of God.

🌑 Femeia care a pășit în iad cu mâinile goale și a scos de acolo 10.000 de copii: un nume aproape șters din istorie, readus la lumină abia după 70 de ani.

🩸 Lagărele în care copilăria era o sentință

În timpul celui de-Al Doilea Război Mondial, Europa devenise un labirint al ororilor.
În zona controlată de regimul fascist Ustaše – Statul Independent al Croației, stat marionetă al Germaniei naziste – lagărele de concentrare se înmulțeau ca niște răni deschise.

Acolo, sârbi, evrei, romi și orice persoană considerată „indezirabilă” erau exterminați sistematic.
Printre ei: mii de copii.

Copii smulși din casele lor, înfometați, izolați, condamnați fără vină.
Iar cei care știau… închideau ochii.
Era prea riscant, prea întunecat, prea fără speranță.

Dar o femeie a privit drept în acel întuneric.

👩‍⚕️ Diana: o mamă, o asistentă, o austriacă într-o țară sfâșiată

Diana Obexer s-a născut în Austria, în anul 1891.
S-a căsătorit cu un medic sârb croat și s-a mutat la Zagreb. Era calmă, discretă, mamă, asistentă medicală calificată – și omul care credea, simplu și direct, că tăcerea în fața răului înseamnă complicitate.

Când a auzit ce se întâmplă în lagăre precum Jasenovac sau Stara Gradiška – locuri pe care supraviețuitorii le compară astăzi cu cel mai crud iad imaginabil – a înțeles că nu putea aștepta ca altcineva „mai potrivit” să intervină.

A decis că îi va salva.

Nu „câțiva”. Nu „pe câți va putea”.
Ci pe toți cei pe care viața îi mai putea atinge.

🕸️ „Acțiunea Dianei”: o rețea clandestină de curaj și ingeniozitate

În 1941, aproape fără să știe cineva în afară de apropiați, Diana a început ceea ce a devenit cunoscut mai târziu ca Acțiunea Budisavljević.

A strâns în jurul ei o rețea de femei curajoase care au decis că nu vor fi spectatoare.
Împreună, ele:
▪ au colectat hrană, medicamente, haine;
▪ au falsificat acte de identitate;
▪ au mituit gardieni și funcționari;
▪ au folosit fiecare legătură umană, fiecare fărâmă de compasiune.

Totul pentru copii care nici nu știau că cineva luptă pentru ei.

🚪 Femeia care a intrat în lagărele morții

Apoi Diana a făcut ceva la limita imposibilului: a cerut – și a obținut – acces în lagăre.

Prin perseverență, inteligență și curaj aproape inimaginabil, a intrat în locuri pe care oamenii încercau să le uite imediat ce le vedeau. A mers în barăci unde mirosul morții era atât de puternic încât rămânea în haine zile întregi. A ținut în brațe copii prea slabi ca să mai poată plânge.

Uneori ieșea cu ei fizic în brațe.
Alteori, cu documente falsificate care le garantau eliberarea.
De fiecare dată, pleca cu o listă precisă de nume – pentru că a înțeles un lucru vital: 
un copil fără identitate poate fi salvat o dată, dar se pierde pentru totdeauna.

Ținea registre în care nota fiecare nume, fiecare familie, fiecare dată.
Aceste caiete aveau să devină, ani mai târziu, unica dovadă a existenței unor copii pe care lumea îi uitase complet.

⚠️ O muncă care putea să o ucidă în orice clipă

Orice vizită, orice negociere, orice gest de ajutor putea să o coste viața.
Dacă ar fi fost descoperită:
▪ ea ar fi fost executată imediat;
▪ rețeaua ei, arestată;
▪ copiii, trimiși înapoi spre moarte.

Și totuși, timp de 4 ani, Diana și voluntarele ei nu s-au oprit niciodată.

👶 Rezultatul: 10.000 de vieți smulse din întuneric

Când războiul s-a încheiat, în 1945, bilanțul era uimitor: peste 10.000 de copii salvați.

Zece mii de copii care altfel ar fi dispărut în tăcere.
Zece mii de destine reconstruite.
Zece mii de oameni care există astăzi pentru că o femeie a refuzat să creadă că e „prea târziu”.

🕳️ Apoi – tăcere. O tăcere programată.

Aici povestea devine aproape la fel de dureroasă ca lagărele în sine.

După război, noul regim al Iugoslaviei a vrut să pună accentul pe unitate, nu pe atrocitățile comise împotriva unui grup anume. Munca Dianei – care scotea în evidență exterminarea sistematică a copiilor sârbi – era considerată incomodă.

Ce s-a întâmplat?
▪ numele ei a fost eliminat din manuale;
▪ registrele ei au fost confiscate și închise în arhive;
▪ meritele operațiunii au fost atribuite altora.

Diana a trăit până în anul 1978, în Zagreb.
În anonimat.
Fără ceremonii. Nici nu a cerut vreuna.
Fără recunoștință publică. Nu a ieșit să se laude cu faptele sale.

Eroina celor 10.000 de copii a murit ca o necunoscută.

📖 Dar adevărul nu rămâne îngropat pentru totdeauna

Abia decenii mai târziu, istoricii au redescoperit caietele Dianei.
Apoi au apărut și cei mai importanți martori: copiii pe care îi salvase, acum adulți în vârstă, care își căutau rădăcinile.

Au povestit despre femeia discretă care:
▪ le-a spus numele când nimeni altcineva nu o făcea;
▪ i-a luat în brațe când nimeni nu îndrăznea;
▪ le-a dat o viață întreagă cu un singur gest: a ales să nu stea deoparte.

În anul 2017, la peste 70 de ani de la sfârșitul războiului, Yad Vashem (instituția care onorează salvatorii Holocaustului) i-a recunoscut sacrificiul și curajul, acordându-i titlul de „Dreaptă între Popoare”.

Astăzi, în Croația, elevii îi învață numele.
Există documentare, monumente, expoziții.
În sfârșit, istoria o spune corect.

🌟 Ce ne lasă Diana?

Nu sloganuri. Nu discursuri. Nu monumente.

Ci o lecție aproape imposibilă: un singur om poate salva mii de vieți.

Fără arme.
Fără protecție.
Fără garanții.

Doar cu:
▪ compasiune;
▪ curaj;
▪ încăpățânarea de a nu accepta răul ca pe o fatalitate.

Diana Budisavljević a intrat în lagărele morții și a ieșit de acolo cu copii în brațe.
Le-a păstrat identitatea când lumea încerca să o șteargă.
A salvat 10.000 de vieți fără să ceară nimic în schimb.

Iar decenii întregi, nimeni nu i-a rostit numele.

Acum, în sfârșit, o facem.
Și nu ar trebui să-l uităm niciodată.

HUGO VICO, MEJOR DEPORTISTA LOCAL EN LA 40ª GALA DEL DEPORTE DE ANDÚJAR

El Salón de Actos de SAFA se vistió de gala para acoger la 40ª edición de la Gala del Deporte de Andújar, una cita ya consolidada que reunió a deportistas, clubes, entidades, empresas y familias para reconocer el esfuerzo y la trayectoria del deporte andujareño. Una gala en la que Hugo Vico García, del Club Arqueros Andújar, fue distinguido como Mejor Deportista Local, valorando su proyección deportiva y su trabajo en el alto rendimiento, en una edición especialmente simbólica por el 40 aniversario de la gala.

Organizada por el Ayuntamiento de Andújar, la Gala del Deporte sirvió para hacer balance de cuatro décadas de historia deportiva y para poner en valor el papel del deporte como elemento de identidad y cohesión social en la ciudad.

Durante el acto, la concejala de Deportes, María José Fuentes, destacó la evolución del deporte en Andújar y la importancia de seguir apostando por los valores deportivos, el deporte inclusivo y el trabajo diario que desarrollan clubes, personal técnico y trabajadores de las instalaciones municipales.

Por su parte, el alcalde, Francisco Carmona, subrayó el papel del deporte como motor educativo y de convivencia, agradeciendo la implicación de deportistas, familias, clubes y empresas que han hecho posible que la Gala del Deporte alcance sus cuatro décadas de trayectoria.

A lo largo de la velada se entregaron galardones en distintas categorías. Susana Martín fue reconocida como Mejor Deportista Provincial por su brillante trayectoria en el pádel; la Peña Iliturgitana del Real Madrid recibió una mención especial en su 40 aniversario; y el Club Andújar Fútbol Sala fue distinguido como Mejor Club Local, coincidiendo también con sus cuatro décadas de historia.

El premio Deporte y Superación recayó en Luciano Díaz, ejemplo de resiliencia y superación personal tras un trasplante renal, mientras que el galardón Deporte y Empresa fue para Casa Azul Boutique Hotel, por su apoyo continuado al deporte local y su implicación en iniciativas deportivas y sociales.

Asimismo, el Club Deportivo Técnicos Al-Ándalus de Huelva fue reconocido como Mejor Club Andaluz tras proclamarse Campeón de España de Fútbol Sala para personas con Discapacidad Intelectual, destacando su labor en favor del deporte inclusivo.

Uno de los momentos más destacados de la noche fue la entrega del premio a Mejor Deportista Andaluz, que recayó en Juan Bautista Castilla “Chamba”, campeón y subcampeón del mundo de Ultraman, referente internacional de la ultrarresistencia y defensor del deporte como estilo de vida.

La Gala del Deporte puso así el broche a una edición muy especial, en la que Andújar volvió a demostrar su firme compromiso con el deporte y con quienes lo hacen posible dentro y fuera de la competición.

St. Lucy is a virgin and martyr of Syracuse in Sicily, whose feast is celebrated on December 13th. According to tradition, Saint Lucy was born to rich and noble parents in the year 283. Her father was of Roman origin, but his early death left her dependent upon her mother, whose name, Eutychia, seems to indicate that she was of Greek heritage.

Like so many of the early martyrs, Lucy had consecrated her virginity to God, and she hoped to devote all her worldly goods to the service of the poor.

Her mother, Eutychia, arranged a marriage for her, but for three years she managed to postpone the marriage. Lucy prayed at the tomb of Saint Agatha to change her mother’s mind about her faith. As a result, her mother's long haemorrhagic illness was cured, and she consented to Lucy's desire to live for God.

Saint Lucy’s rejected bridegroom, Paschasius, denounced Lucy as a Christian. The governor planned to force her into prostitution, but when guards went to fetch her, they could not move her even when they hitched her to a team of oxen. The governor ordered her to be killed instead.

After a gruesome torture which included having her eyes torn out, she was surrounded by bundles of wood which were set afire, but the fire quickly died out. She prophesied against her persecutors, and was then executed by being stabbed to death with a dagger.

According to later accounts, Lucy warned Paschasius he would be punished. When the governor heard this he ordered the guards to gouge out her eyes; however, in another telling, it was Lucy who removed her eyes in an attempt to discourage a persistent suitor who greatly admired them. When her body was being prepared for burial, they discovered her eyes had been restored. This and the meaning of her name ("light" or "lucid") led to her patronage with eyes; the blind, eye trouble, and other eye ailments.

That evening, a message arrived in the family group chat:

“Please pray for us.
Our daughter has turned away.
We don’t recognize her anymore.”

Attached was a photo of her parents kneeling in prayer.

Maria’s chest tightened.

Maria’s Internal Battle

The silence was hard.

Every instinct screamed:

Fix it.
Explain.
Make them comfortable again.

But instead, Maria sat with the discomfort.

She cried quietly.
She paced her room.
She prayed — not the fearful prayers she was taught, but honest ones.

“God… if You’re really love, help me not break myself to keep others whole.”

And slowly, something unexpected happened.

The panic didn’t come.

The guilt rose —
but it didn’t drown her.

Snippets from HIC Dawah Class where we looked into Jihād in the Modern Lens 
 

Jihād, in its true Islamic sense, means striving in the cause of Allah. 

Jihad is a broad concept that includes striving with one’s life, wealth, resources, and speech, all in obedience to Allah and within the boundaries set by Allah.

There are three major forms of inner and ethical striving:

 Jihād al-Nafs – striving against one’s own desires, weaknesses, and inclinations toward sin.

 Jihād against Shayṭān – resisting temptation, doubt, and misguidance inspired by Satan.

 Jihād against hypocrisy (Munāfiqūn) – confronting hypocrisy through truth, sincerity, and upright conduct.

Jihād is generally classified as Farḍ Kifāyah (a collective obligation). This means that if a sufficient number of Muslims undertake it properly, the obligation is lifted from the rest of the community.

Participation in physical Jihād is required only from Muslims who meet certain conditions, including:

Physical fitness and sound health.

Adequate capability and training in the use of arms and necessary equipment.

Islam places strict ethical and legal controls on Jihād and ensures that it is never based on aggression, injustice, or personal motives.

Jihad should solely be based on the preservation of faith, justice, and human dignity.

The Arabic name of Almería during al-Andalus was:

الْمَرِيَّة
al-Mariyya

More fully, it was often called:

الْمَرِيَّة البَجَّانَة
al-Mariyya al-Bajjāna

Meaning & context
 • al-Mariyya comes from maraʾā (مرأى), meaning “the watchtower” or “the lookout”, because it originally served as the port and coastal watch post for the nearby city of Bayyāna (Pechina).
 • Over time, al-Mariyya grew in importance and eventually surpassed Bayyāna, becoming a major naval, commercial, and textile center in al-Andalus.

The Andalus era refers to the period between 711 and 1492, when large parts of the Iberian Peninsula—present-day Spain and Portugal—were under North African rule, known historically as Al-Andalus. This era represents one of the most intellectually vibrant and culturally transformative periods in European history.

A central and often underrecognized role in the formation and success of Al-Andalus was played by Amazigh (Berber) North Africans, who formed the backbone of the initial conquest and the long-term settlement of the region. These Amazigh communities, originating from present-day Morocco, Algeria, and the broader Maghreb, brought with them deep traditions of engineering, mathematics, astronomy, agriculture, and architecture, which profoundly shaped Iberian civilization.

Al-Andalus became a bridge of knowledge between the Islamic world and Europe. Amazigh scholars, administrators, and craftsmen participated in a multilingual intellectual ecosystem where Arabic, Latin, Hebrew, and Amazigh oral traditions coexisted.

The Amazigh contribution to Al-Andalus stands as a testament to how mobility, knowledge exchange, and cultural plurality can generate enduring progress. Their legacy remains embedded in Iberian cities, agricultural landscapes, scientific thought, and architectural heritage—long after the political end of Al-Andalus.

Ang **munaafiq (mapagkunwari)** ay taong nagpapakita na Muslim siya ngunit sa loob ng puso niya ay hindi tunay ang pananampalataya. Narito ang **mga palatandaan (signs) ng munaafiq** ayon sa **Hadith at Qur’an**:

# 📌 **Mga Palatandaan ng Munaafiq (Ayon sa Hadith)**

Sinabi ng Propeta Muhammad ﷺ:

> **“Tatlo ang palatandaan ng munaafiq:**
> **kapag nagsalita siya, nagsisinungaling;
> kapag nangako siya, binabali niya;
> at kapag pinagkatiwalaan siya, nagtataksil siya.”**
> *(Sahih al-Bukhari at Muslim)*

At sa ibang Hadith:

> **“Apat na katangian: kung taglay niya ang lahat nito, siya ay ganap na munaafiq; at kung may isa rito, may katangian siya ng nifaq hanggang iwan niya ito:**
>
> * kapag pinagkatiwalaan, nagtataksil
> * kapag nagsalita, nagsisinungaling
> * kapag nangako, hindi tinutupad
> * kapag nakikipagtalo, lumalampas sa hangganan”*
>   *(Sahih Muslim)*

-# 📌 **Mga Palatandaan ng Munaafiq (Ayon sa Qur’an)**

🔸 **Tamad sa pagsalah**

> *“Kapag tumatayo sila para magdasal, ginagawa nila ito nang tamad at para lang makita ng mga tao.”*
> *(Qur’an 4:142)*

December 31: FBI taking on public corruption 

As we wrap up 2025, your @FBI has an update for you on our efforts to crush public corruption and restore trust in federal law enforcement.

This is one of the most important efforts we’ve undertaken at the Bureau. You deserve to have confidence in your public officials - and to know that justice will be applied without fear or favor. That has not been the case in recent history. We have been working day and night to rebuild that confidence.

These are very much ongoing investigations - much of which we cannot discuss publicly out of respect for the investigative process, Constitutional presumption of innocence, and the judicial process. Equally - there are many public corruption investigations going on as we speak that the public may know very little about - or even none at all. 

In less than a year, here is some of what we’ve undertaken:

-James Comey, former FBI Director, indicted for allegedly lying to Congress during a 2020 Congressional hearing. This is an ongoing case.

-Leticia James, New York AG, indicted in October for allegedly committing bank fraud and making false statements to a financial institution. 

-Judge Hannah Dugan out of Wisconsin, indicted and convicted for felony obstruction - impeding federal immigration authorities attempting to detain an illegal immigrant. The Judge is awaiting sentencing.

-In Mississippi, 20 indictments - including 14 Mississippi current and former law enforcement officials - on charges of drug trafficking and bribery.

-Linda Sun, a former senior aide to Governors Kathy Hochul and Andrew Cuomo in New York, indicted for allegedly taking bribes from China. This is an ongoing trial. 

-U.S. Representative Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, indicted on multiple federal charges including money laundering and conspiracy to steal federal disaster funds.

-Former Ambassador John Bolton, indicted on 18 federal charges, including unlawful retention and transmission of classified material.

-In the Minnesota fraud investigation, 78 indicted, 57 convicted in the investigation of public corruption and misuse of taxpayer funds. Between late May 2025 and December 2025, we have had 16 open investigations into approximately 32 healthcare and homecare providers accused of fraud. This remains very much an ongoing investigation. 

-Dana Williamson, Governor Gavin Newsom’s former chief of staff, indicted on federal public corruption charges including conspiracy to commit wire fraud and bank fraud. 

-New Orleans Mayor Latoya Cantrell, indicted on 11 federal charges for allegedly misusing public funds.

-Even here, at your FBI, we dismantled the corrupt CR-15 squad that had been caught blatantly weaponizing law enforcement and politically targeting individuals. That unit no longer exists, and those responsible have been removed.

Dismantling public corruption is a top priority of our leadership team here - we’ve worked day and night on that mission and will continue to do so until justice is done.

Abdullahi Osman Mohamed, oo sidoo kale loo yaqaanno Ismaaciil Injineer wuxuu ahaa hoggaamiye sare oo ka tirsan kooxda Al-Shabaab, wuxu ahaa xeel dheere khibrad iyo waayo aragnimo u lahaa agabka qarxyada sidoo kalana wuxuu ahaa garabka iclaamka ee Al-Kataa'ib. Injineerka wuxuu 1983 ku dhashay Muqdisho, wuxuu ka soo jeedaa Hiiraan wuxuuna si rasmi ah ugu dhuumaaleysan jiray jubooyinka sida: Jilib, Saakow, iyo Kuunya Barrow. Injinrerka sidoo kale wuxuu qeyb muhiim ah ka ahaa garabka warbaahinta Al-Shabaab ee al-Kataa'ib laga soo bilaabo 2008, isagoo markii dambe noqday madaxa guud ee garabka warbaahinta 2020.

Injineerka Sannadkii 2014, wuxuu xubin ka noqday qaybta farsamaynta qaraxyadda, isagoo maamulayay xarumo ku kala yaalla Jilib, Saakoow, iyo Kuunyo-Barrow. Waxaa la xaqiijiyay inuu hoggaamiye u ahaa koox ka kooban 68 xubnood oo qaabilsanayd qaraxyada. Injineerka wuxuu ahaa la-taliye gaar ah oo u dhow amiirka al-Shabaab Axmad Diiriye oo loo yaqaano Abuu Cubeyda. Waxaa la rumeysan yahay inuu maamuli jiray qul-qul dhaqaale oo gaaraya $6 milyan oo dollar sannadkii, taas oo loo isticmaali jiray agabka qaraxyada sida: Soo iibin, rakibaad, farsamo, soogudbin iyo qarxin intaba. Sababo la xiriira khatarta uu ku leeyahay amniga gobolka, Injineerka ayaa wajahay in baadi goobkiisa lacag la duldhigo.

Waaxda arrimaha dibadda ee Maraykanka ayaa u aqoonsatay argagixiye Caalami ah oo si gaar ah loo calaamadeeyay. Injineerka May 2023 golaha ammaanka ee Q.M ayaa ku daray liiska cunaqabataynta ee dadka khatarta ku ah xasilloonida Soomaaliya iyo Kenya. Juun 2023 barnaamijka abaal marinta cadaaladda (Rewards for Justice) ee Maraykanka ayaa ballan-qaaday $5 milyan oo dollar oo la siinayo cid kasta oo keenta xog horseedi karta in la qabto ama la khaarijiyo Ismaaciil Injineer. Injineerka kaliya ma aheyn xubin caadi ah, wuxuu ahaa mid ka mid ah maskaxda ka dambaysa awoodda farsamo ee qaraxyada iyo midda dacaayada warbaahinta ee Al-Shabaab.

A 12th-century biographical dictionary of Andalusian scholars, written by Ibn Bashkuwal roughly 100-200 years after her death, records: "She excelled in writing, grammar, and poetry. Her knowledge of mathematics was also immense and she was proficient in other sciences as well. There were none in the Umayyad palace as noble as her."
That's the primary source. That's what a medieval scholar thought worth recording.
From this foundation, an elaborate structure has been built. In modern retellings, Lubna becomes a mathematician, astronomer, and linguist. She masters Arabic, Latin, Greek, and Hebrew. She oversees a library of 500,000 volumes. She travels to Cairo, Damascus, and Baghdad to acquire rare manuscripts. She leads teams of copyists and scholars. She establishes schools and teaches street children mathematics.
Some of this may be true. Much of it is speculation or embellishment.
Writer Kamila Shamsie, who produced a BBC Radio 3 episode about Lubna for a series on the Islamic Golden Age, has noted the problems with the accumulated narrative. If Lubna was the Caliph's personal secretary—as sources agree—she could not simultaneously have been traveling across the Middle East for months at a time to acquire books. The book-acquisition story may actually belong to another woman, possibly named Fatima, whose achievements were merged with Lubna's by historians who couldn't imagine two female intellectuals at the same court.
Shamsie concludes: "What does seem clear about Lubna of Cordoba is that she was connected to both the palace and the world of books during the reign of al-Hakam II, and was significant enough to be remembered for her intellect and learning."
That's the modest, honest version. It's still remarkable.
Consider the context. Lubna was born enslaved—one of thousands of enslaved people in Córdoba during this period. The caliph's palace harem contained many enslaved women, some of whom bore children by the caliph. One theory suggests Lubna's father may have been Caliph Abd al-Rahman III himself, which would explain her unusual access to education.
She was not simply a talented woman whose brilliance was "recognized and nurtured." She was a person who rose from bondage through circumstances we can only speculate about—talent, certainly, but also the particular structures of power in a slave-owning society where some enslaved people could be educated, freed, and elevated to positions of trust.
The library of Córdoba was real and genuinely impressive. Al-Hakam II was a renowned patron of learning who reportedly sent agents throughout the Islamic world to acquire manuscripts. The claim that the library held 400,000 or 500,000 volumes may be legendary—the numbers come from later sources—but Córdoba was genuinely one of the great intellectual centers of the medieval world.
In 2019, a street in Córdoba was named "Avenida Escriba Lubna"—Scribe Lubna Avenue—as part of a project to recognize women in the city's history. The artist José Luis Muñoz painted her portrait for a permanent exhibition at La Casa de Sefarad. She appears on Judy Chicago's installation The Dinner Party.
She has become, in other words, a symbol—of learned women in Islamic history, of female accomplishment against the odds, of a golden age we want to remember. These are worthy things to symbolize.
But when we turn a fragmentary historical figure into a fully realized character—complete with detailed accomplishments, motivations, and a satisfying narrative arc—we risk losing something important. We risk losing the honesty about how little we know, and how much of history consists of gaps, silences, and speculation.
What we know about Lubna of Córdoba: she was enslaved, freed, learned, praised. She worked with books in a palace. She was remembered.
That's enough. That's already extraordinary. The embellishments, however well-intentioned, don't make her more real. They make her less so.

En lugar de simplemente hacer una donación, Camilo decidió ofrecer un concierto para recaudar fondos para la causa. Se puso en contacto con Manolo Sánchez y juntos, junto con Pepe Domingo Castaño, José María García, Vicente Marco y otros, hicieron que el evento fuera un éxito.

En cuanto se anunció en la radio, las entradas se agotaron en un par de horas. La víspera del concierto, en la "madrugada de la Cadena SER", se hizo un especial para vender la simbólica "fila 0" y álbumes de "Entre amigos", para recaudar más fondos. Camilo contaba: "La gente respondió perfectamente a mi llamada. Julio Iglesias llamó desde Munich y compró uno en cincuenta mil, Manolo Escobar acudió a la emisora y llevó otro en veinticinco mil, La “Chana”, Pedro Ruiz, Mary Carmen Izquierdo, Encarna Polo, Maria Albarracin, Ana Belén, Pablo Abraira, Alfonso del Real, Alcatraz... No sé cuántos, no puedo recordar a todos ahora mismo, pero se volcaron. En la Discoteca “Long Play” Paco Santos y José María Suárez subastaron cosas para echar una mano y aportaron otro buen pico."

En total se recaudaron más de dos millones de pesetas, fue un concierto maravilloso donde Camilo actuó acompañado por el grupo Alcatraz y recibió magníficas críticas de la prensa por su calidad artística. Una vez más Camilo dió muestra de su corazón tan inmenso, de su gran generosidad y compasión por el prójimo. ¡Bravo por Camilo y por todos los que colaboraron en esta noble causa! 🙏 Su legado va más allá de su música, es un ejemplo de solidaridad y bondad que inspira a todos. 😊

MPF mendakwa komander tersebut sebelum ini berkhidmat sebagai komander Organisasi Perlindungan Maklumat LEC Iranshahr serta telah membunuh “pekerja bahan api Baloch” dalam beberapa bulan kebelakangan ini. [22]

MPF sebelum ini memberi amaran pada 1 Januari bahawa mereka akan bertindak balas terhadap “setiap peluru” yang ditembak oleh pasukan keselamatan Iran ke arah penunjuk perasaan. [23]

CTP-ISW belum merekodkan sebarang protes di Iranshahr setakat masa penulisan ini. Serangan MPF pada 7 Januari menandakan kali pertama MPF melakukan serangan di Iranshahr.

MPF sebelum ini melakukan serangan pertamanya di Zahedan, wilayah Sistan dan Baluchistan, pada awal Disember 2025. [24]

Media antirejim dan pengguna media sosial dakwa bahawa militia Iraq yang disokong Iran telah dikerahkan ke Iran bagi menyokong tindakan keras rejim terhadap protes. [25]

CTP-ISW tidak dapat mengesahkan laporan ini, dan media antirejim telah menyebarkan laporan serupa semasa gelombang protes sebelum ini.

Media antirejim Iran International lapor pada 6 Januari, sekitar 800 pejuang militia Iraq yang disokong Iran dikerahkan ke Iran sejak 2 Januari melalui lintasan sempadan di Diyala, Maysan, dan Basra, berdasarkan “maklumat” tanpa sumber. [26]

Pejuang Iraq itu dilaporkan merupakan anggota Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada, dan Pertubuhan Badr, antara militia lain. [27]

Iran International menambah bahawa pegawai kerajaan Iraq yang tidak dinyatakan identitinya menyedari tentang penempatan pejuang tersebut, yang dilakukan atas nama lawatan ziarah ke Makam Imam Reza di Mashhad, Iran. [28]

Militia Iraq yang disokong Iran kerap menggunakan kawalan mereka ke atas banyak lintasan sempadan Iran-Iraq untuk menyeludup barangan seperti senjata keluar dan masuk Iraq. [29]

Beberapa pengguna media sosial juga mendakwa sejak beberapa hari kebelakangan ini bahawa anggota Pasukan Mobilisasi Popular (PMF) yang disokong Iran menekan protes di Iran, termasuk di Bandar Hamedan, wilayah Hamedan. [30]

PMF ialah perkhidmatan keselamatan negara Iraq yang merangkumi banyak militia Iraq yang disokong Iran yang cenderung melapor kepada Iran dan bukan kepada perdana menteri Iraq. [31]

Jika benar, penempatan militia tersebut boleh kukuhkan usaha rejim untuk mengekang protes.

Militia Iraq mungkin juga lebih bersedia menggunakan keganasan atau kekerasan maut terhadap penunjuk perasaan, memandangkan mereka tidak mempunyai hubungan peribadi dengan komuniti Iran yang memprotes.

Media antirejim sering menyebarkan laporan mengenai penempatan pasukan proksi Iran ke Iran untuk menindas protes ketika waktu pergolakan.

Sebagai contoh, Iran International memetik media Israel pada 2022 mendakwa bahawa militia Iraq yang disokong Iran di bawah PMF telah dikerahkan ke Iran semasa gerakan Mahsa Amini bagi membantu rejim Iran mengekang protes. [32]

Bekas ketua Mahkamah Revolusi Tehran, Musa Ghazanfarabadi, pernah beri bayangan kepada pelajar agama Iran di Qom pada 2019 bahawa kumpulan Paksi Penentangan — termasuk militia Iraq yang disokong Iran — boleh sokong rejim dalam menekan gerakan protes di Iran. [33]

Pasukan keselamatan Iran turut bantu PMF kekang protes secara ganas di Iraq pada 2019. [34]

ORA TRUMP DÀ LA CACCIA A KHAMENEI. LE “AQUILE URLANTI” NEI CIELI DEL CONFINE. REGIME AL TRAMONTO?

Mariano Giustino su Il Riformista dell' 8 Gennaio 2026 

Le “aquile urlanti” di Trump starebbero dando la caccia a Khamenei. La 101ª Brigata aviotrasportata statunitense e la Delta Force è segnalata in operazioni al confine iraniano. Da alcuni giorni aerei e rifornitori Usa sono in movimento. Un’intensa attività logistica tra Stati Uniti, Europa e Medio Oriente si registra al confine tra Iran e Iraq con decine di aerocisterne per il rifornimento in volo e aerei da trasporto strategico. Dopo la cattura di Maduro e i chiari moniti di Trump con la minaccia di un intervento contro il regime iraniano se dovesse continuare ad usare violenza contro i manifestanti, Washington sta rafforzando la propria postura militare nella regione.

Numerosi velivoli della United States Air Force, inclusi aerei da trasporto pesante C-5 e C-17, sarebbero decollati sia dagli Stati Uniti che da una base americana nel Regno Unito, dirigendosi in Iraq al confine con l’Iran. Questo trasferimento in corso di forze e mezzi in un’area già ad altissima tensione, fa pensare seriamente a preparativi per possibili imminenti attacchi contro l’Iran oppure ad un modo per tenere sotto minaccia il regime mentre i manifestanti invadono le città iraniane lottando per liberare il paese dalla Repubblica islamica: si tratterebbe di uno scudo militare sui cieli iraniani a protezione della popolazione che è insorta.

Ormai, a 12 giorni dal loro inizio, le proteste dilagano come in fiume in piena in tutte le province iraniane e soprattutto nei distretti industriali del paese, dal tessile a quello portuale e degli idrocarburi e del cemento. Il popolo iraniano, dai mercanti dei bazar ai giovani universitari, dai lavoratori ai pensionati e persino ex funzionari del regime vogliono la fine della Repubblica islamica. La popolazione ribattezza le strade di Teheran sostituendo le targhe della toponomastica con le scritte “Via del Presidente Trump”.

La caduta di Maduro è uno shock geopolitico indiretto per Teheran; uno shock che chiude i canali finanziari dei pasdaran, che segna la fine di “Hezbollah Venezuela” e pone fine alle manovre strategiche della Repubblica islamica di espansione in America Latina. Sono almeno 50 i morti in oltre 300 manifestazioni in 92 città di 30 province; almeno 2.076, sono i cittadini arrestati, centinaia le sparizioni forzate e, quotidiane, le impiccagioni. Eppure la popolazione non ha rinunciato alla lotta di liberazione. La violenza da parte delle forze paramilitari basij e delle milizie jihadiste assoldate dal regime si è estesa fin dentro gli ospedali.

È in corso la caccia all’oppositore. Manifestanti disarmati sono corsi all’ospedale Sina di Teheran, in fuga dalle forze di sicurezza. I basij hanno fatto irruzione nella struttura sanitaria e hanno lanciato gas lacrimogeni all’interno di essa e arrestato i manifestanti feriti. Anche a Malekshahi, nella provincia di Ilam, le forze del regime hanno aperto il fuoco vivo sui civili, poi hanno attaccato l’ospedale e rapito i manifestanti feriti. Si è scatenato l’inferno nella metropolitana di Teheran. I basij hanno sparato decine di lacrimogeni all’interno delle stazioni. Le unità motociclistiche dei paramilitari controllano rigorosamente tutti gli ingressi e le uscite.

Gruppi di manifestanti attaccano gli agenti del regime con la tattica “mordi e fuggi”. Il piano della Repubblica islamica di sedare le proteste sin dal loro insorgere al momento è fallito anche perché vi sarebbero delle defezioni all’interno dell’apparato paramilitare e dei guardiani della rivoluzione. Le forze della repressione non sembrano molto determinate a reprimere le manifestazioni che in alcuni casi assumono caratteristiche violente. Per questo il regime sta facendo ricorso a milizie mercenarie irachene, afgane e libanesi. Circa 800 miliziani sciiti iracheni sono stati inviati in Iran per reprimere la popolazione in rivolta. Le milizie irachene affiliate al regime iraniano di Kata’ib Hezbollah, Harkat al-Nujaba, Sayyid al-Shuhada e Badr sono impiegate in prima linea per la brutale repressione dei manifestanti.

Il processo di trasferimento di queste forze viene effettuato attraverso i tre valichi di frontiera di Shalamcheh, Chazhabeh e Khosravi, e la sua copertura ufficiale è descritta come un “pellegrinaggio ai luoghi sacri dell’Imam Reza a Mashhad”, ma in realtà queste forze si radunano nella base di Khamenei ad Ahvaz e vengono poi inviate in varie regioni per partecipare alla più violenta repressione delle proteste, mai messe in atto finora. I miliziani catturano i manifestanti che vengono trasportati in località segrete. Si registrano centinaia di sparizioni forzate. Intanto dai campus univeristari di tutto il paese si leva un solo grido: “Via la Repubblica islamica dall’Iran”.

How the British Left Dismisses Iran's Uprising: The Campist Playbook

Source: https://open.substack.com/pub/redmole/p/how-the-british-left-dismisses-irans?utm_source=direct&utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=web 

Disclaimer: The views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of IASWI.

The message arrived in a left WhatsApp group on January 6th, 2026. A member asked if anyone had “a source for what’s actually happening in Iran,” having seen reports of mass protests on Instagram. Within minutes, the replies crystallised a worldview:
“There are legitimate protests against Iran’s government but to my understanding they are vastly less than is being reported. The common belief is that there are foreign agitators organising some of the anti-government protests in the interests of the usual suspects USA and Israel.”
Craig Murray, the former diplomat turned left commentator, weighed in: “I don’t buy it. Exactly the same narrative as we got over the toppling of Assad. And what has been the result? Israel occupying southern Syria and Southern Lebanon and the new Zionist leader of Syria feted in the White House.”
Another participant agreed: “Bears very little resemblance from what I’m hearing from back home and follows the same old narrative which should now be very clearly recognized as propaganda.”
This is the campist reflex in its grassroots form. Before any serious examination of what is happening in Iran, before any engagement with the demands of Iranian workers and students, the left-wing instinct is to ask: who benefits? And if the answer might be Washington or Tel Aviv, to dismiss the entire phenomenon as manufactured.
The problem is that people are dying. The receipts exist. And the British left’s refusal to read them constitutes a political betrayal.
Ten Days that Shook Iran

The protests that erupted across Iran on December 28th, 2025 were triggered by the Pezeshkian administration’s abolition of the 28,500-toman preferential exchange rate: a subsidised system used for importing basic goods.1 The immediate effect was a tarifazo, a shock price hike that sent bread and fuel costs through the roof in a country where annualised inflation had already reached 52%.2
This was not a colour revolution manufactured in Langley. It was a bread riot with political characteristics, emerging from material conditions that no amount of “foreign agitator” rhetoric can explain away.
The numbers tell the story. By late 2024, over 57% of the Iranian population experienced malnourishment.3 By early January 2026, the rial had collapsed to 1.46 million against the dollar. Capital flight since 2018 totalled $116 billion.4 The military and security budget increased by 150% while public sector wages were adjusted by only 20%: less than half the inflation rate.5 When meat becomes a luxury and medicine prices double, people take to the streets. They do not require instructions from the CIA.
By January 6th, the tenth day of the uprising, protests had spread to over 110 cities across 27 of Iran’s 31 provinces.6 Unlike the 2022 “Woman, Life, Freedom” movement, which concentrated in major urban centres and Kurdish regions, this uprising is particularly strong in medium-sized towns and rural areas. The geographical spread indicates something the campist analysis cannot accommodate: a poly-crisis in which the regime’s capacity to impose control has fractured across the periphery.
The regime’s response tells its own story. At least 36 people have been killed, including four minors, and over 2,000 arrested.7 On January 4th, Revolutionary Guards raided the Imam Khomeini Hospital in Ilam City, using shotguns and tear gas inside the hospital grounds, smashing glass doors to drag wounded protesters directly from their beds.8 Reports indicate that approximately 800 members of Iranian-backed Iraqi Shiite militias, including Kataib Hezbollah and the Badr Organization, have been deployed to assist in suppression: evidence that the regime fears defections within its own security forces.9
The dominant slogans are not “Bring Back the Shah.” They are: “Neither Shah nor Supreme Leader: democracy and equality” and “Death to the oppressor, be it the Shah or the Supreme Leader.”10 And this one, which should give the campist left pause: “Not for Gaza, not for Lebanon, I give my life for Iran.”11 The Iranian masses are explicitly rejecting the regime’s expenditure on regional proxy wars. They are not asking for permission from the “axis of resistance.”
The Monarchist Trap

The campist left has seized on the figure of Reza Pahlavi II, the Shah’s son, as evidence that the protests serve imperialist interests. One WhatsApp participant noted seeing “photos of the Shah’s son at the Wailing Wall a couple of days ago with quotes about his love for Israel. Nothing like it to make one assume CIA/Mossad at work.”
The assumption is understandable. It is also wrong.
Trotskyist researchers have documented that much of the “pro-monarchy” element in current protests is manufactured: not by Western intelligence, but by the Islamic Republic itself. Reports indicate that plainclothes IRGC and Basij agents have been sent into crowds to chant pro-Pahlavi slogans as a divide-and-rule strategy, designed to hijack the anti-regime narrative and suggest that the only alternative to the mullahs is restoration of the old dictatorship.12 Iranians have exposed deepfake videos and recycled footage from 2022 using voice-overs to falsely suggest protesters are calling for the Shah.13
The Fourth International’s French section warns against “attempts at recuperation” by monarchist currents, describing Pahlavi’s programme as “authoritarian and ultraliberal” and noting that his supporters have manipulated protest videos.14The regime and the monarchists share an interest in erasing the third option: independent working-class power.
The British Campist Response

How has the British left responded to this uprising? The pattern is now familiar from Ukraine, from Syria, from every case where genuine popular resistance inconveniently targets a regime that opposes Western imperialism.
Stop the War Coalition has framed the uprising primarily as a precursor to Western intervention. On January 5th, 2026, National Convenor Lindsey German published “Trump’s Return to Colonial Conquest,” which subordinates the Iranian protests entirely to the threat of American military action.
German acknowledges, in passing, that the regime is “repressive and authoritarian.” But her analytical energy is directed elsewhere: “It is up to the Iranian people to decide how to deal with that, not the discredited monarchists and their friends the imperialists.”15
Note the grammar. The Iranian people are granted agency in the abstract, then immediately disappeared. The only concrete actors in German’s framing are “monarchists” and “imperialists.” The workers facing 52% inflation, the women demanding freedom, the students with “nothing left to lose”: they exist only as a passive mass at risk of being “hijacked” by foreign powers. The possibility that they might be political subjects with their own demands and capacities does not register.
Craig Murray has been more explicit. In a December 2024 interview with The National, following the collapse of the Assad regime, Murray described the Syrian government as “flawed but pluralist.”16
Let that phrase settle. A regime that barrel-bombed Aleppo, used chemical weapons on Ghouta, and operated an industrial torture apparatus at Saydnaya prison was, in Murray’s telling, “pluralist.” The word has been evacuated of meaning; it now signifies nothing more than “opposed to Israel.”
Murray applies the same framework to Iran. The 2026 protests represent “exactly the same narrative” used to topple Assad, he argues: a “fraudulent” pretext for “Greater Israel” and US regional dominance.17 The material conditions, the economic triggers, the documented scale of mobilisation: none of this penetrates the analysis. If Western media reports it, it must be propaganda.
George Galloway has used his platform to host Prof. Seyed Mohammad Marandi, a prominent defender of the Islamic Republic, to discuss whether Washington is “preparing for confrontation.”18 His commentary focuses on the “collapse of international law” and frames the protests within the regime’s own narrative: an external attempt to “strike at the axis of resistance.”
David Miller and Chris Williamson, co-hosting Palestine Declassified on Iranian state broadcaster Press TV, have described the protests as part of a “Zionist and imperialist propaganda” effort intended to destroy the “multi-polar world.”19 Miller characterises internal dissent within the “axis of resistance” as an “epistemic alliance” against the liberal order: academic jargon deployed to dismiss hunger and repression as Western fabrication.
When Ali Khamenei claimed that “rioters” were being “incited or hired by the enemy,” Miller echoed the framing.20 The Supreme Leader’s word, apparently, requires no verification.
The More Defensible Positions

Not all British left coverage has been equally bankrupt.
The Morning Star has provided reporting that at least acknowledges the class dynamics. The paper cites the Committee for the Defence of the Iranian People’s Rights (CODIR) and the Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA), platforming Iranian trade unionists and students and framing the crisis as “budgetary apartheid.”21This represents a more critical stance toward the “corrupt theocracy” than the paper adopted during the Syrian collapse.
Socialist Worker has published more detailed analysis of the economic triggers, explicitly citing the subsidy abolition and hyperinflation. The paper interviewed an activist using the pseudonym “Sahar” from Iranians for Palestine UK, who emphasised that the revolt represents a “root-level demand” from a generation with “nothing left to lose.”22
Sahar’s framing deserves attention: “Any Western intervention and posturing that they’re on the side of Iranians undermines the sovereignty of Iranians.”23 This is the correct position. It opposes intervention while defending the uprising’s legitimacy. Socialist Worker uses Sahar to bridge support for the “right to revolt” with opposition to “imperialist hijacking,” platforming an Iranian voice that validates the class struggle while condemning Trump’s “rescue” rhetoric.
The Socialist Party (CWI) has been sharper still. In a January 7th analysis, Scott Hunter characterised the protests as a “lightning rod for accumulated anger against the Islamic Republic regime: a deeply reactionary theocracy: and the dire state of Iranian capitalism.”24 The Socialist Party argues that while Western imperialists would prefer a “colour change” that preserves capitalism, there is no prospect of sustained improvement under capitalism in Iran. They call for the working class to enter the movement en masse to lead the overthrow of both the theocracy and “dead-end capitalism.”
The International Socialist Alternative (ISA) has called for “democratic committees of action” to be formed in communities to resist state attacks, emphasising continuity with the 2022 “Woman, Life, Freedom” movement.25
The Revolutionary Communist Internationalhas been notably quiet on Iran, prioritising the Venezuela crisis. Their January 3rd statement clarified that opposition to imperialist attacks “no more expressed support for the corrupt and reactionary regime of the mullahs in Tehran” than their Venezuela position expressed confidence in Maduro.26 The framing is correct but the emphasis is revealing: Venezuela gets the mobilisation; Iran gets the footnote.
The Internationalist Alternative

What does genuine solidarity look like?
Hands Off the People of Iran (HOPI), led by Yassamine Mather, provides the sharpest contrast to the campist bloc. On January 2nd, 2026, Mather and the Cooperation Council of Iranian Left and Communist Forces issued a statement titled “Forward to the revolution!” calling for the “revolutionary overthrow of the Islamic Republic.”27
In the Weekly Worker, Mather argues that the regime is in “survival mode” and that the uprising represents a “fusion of bread and freedom” that cannot be managed through social concessions.28 She remains vocally critical of those on the left who “refuse to show solidarity” with internal struggles because they fear being labelled “terrorist supporters” or aiding imperialism.
Anti-Capitalist Resistance, part of the British section of the Fourth International, has critiqued the campist position directly, arguing that reducing “global struggle” to “only the crimes of US imperialism” ignores “the agency of real people.”29
The Fourth International itself characterises the 2026 uprising as a “new phase” synthesising the socio-economic demands of 2018-2019 with the aspirations for equality and freedom from 2022’s “Woman, Life, Freedom” movement.30 Their analysis centres a crucial point: the Iranian people “do not want to choose between two despotisms.” They reject Trump and Netanyahu’s plans to impose solutions “from above” while equally rejecting the theocratic regime’s claim to anti-imperialist credentials.
The FI identifies the organised working class: teachers, nurses, truck drivers, oil and gas workers: as the “beating heart of Iran’s economy” with the unique power to topple the regime through independent struggle.31 This is the perspective the campist left cannot articulate, because it requires recognising Iranian workers as subjects rather than objects of history.
Most damningly, the FI explicitly critiques the segment of the left that supports the Iranian regime due to its hostility toward the US and Israel. This campist position, they argue, “denies the right of Iranian workers and the oppressed to resist after decades of suffering under the boot of a capitalist dictatorship with Islamic colouring.”32
The Pattern

We have seen this before. On Ukraine, the campist left dismissed the Maidan movement as a fascist coup, then struggled to explain why millions of Ukrainians were resisting Russian invasion. On Syria, they dismissed the revolution as a jihadist conspiracy, then had nothing to say when Assad’s regime collapsed from internal rot. Now Iran.
The analytical method is consistent. When confronted with a popular uprising against a regime that opposes Western imperialism, the campist reflex is to:
1. Question the scale (”vastly less than is being reported”)
2. Attribute agency to foreign powers (”foreign agitators,” “usual suspects”)
3. Identify any reactionary element within the opposition and treat it as representative (”discredited monarchists”)
4. Frame solidarity with the uprising as support for intervention
5. Platform regime voices as authoritative sources
The result is a left that cannot recognise working-class struggle when it occurs in the wrong geopolitical configuration. Iranian workers facing 57% malnourishment are not subjects with demands; they are pawns in a great-power chess game, their agency dissolved into the machinations of Washington and Tel Aviv.
Craig Murray’s description of Assad’s Syria as “flawed but pluralist” reveals where this logic terminates. Any regime, however brutal, can be rehabilitated if it stands opposed to the correct enemies. The torture chambers at Saydnaya become “flaws.” The hunger in Tehran becomes “propaganda.”
The Task

The Fourth International’s position remains what it has always been: unconditional opposition to imperialist intervention, complete political independence from the regime, solidarity with the workers’ own organisations.
This means opposing any US or Israeli military action against Iran. It means rejecting sanctions that immiserate the population while strengthening the regime’s grip. It means refusing to platform monarchist grifters or their imperialist backers.
But it also means recognising that Iranian workers have the right to resist “decades of suffering under the boot of a capitalist dictatorship with Islamic colouring.” It means taking seriously the slogans on the streets: “Neither Shah nor Supreme Leader.” It means understanding that the main enemy of the Iranian working class is, first and foremost, the regime that arrests trade unionists, disappears activists, and shoots protesters.
The campist left has made its choice. When confronted with a genuine popular uprising, they reached for the playbook: foreign agitators, Zionist propaganda, colour revolution. They chose geopolitical alignment over working-class solidarity.
The rest of us have a different choice to make. We can stand with the Iranian workers, students, and women who are risking their lives for bread and freedom. Or we can stand with Craig Murray’s “flawed but pluralist” despotisms, waiting for a revolution that meets our geopolitical approval.
The receipts are in. The uprising is real. The only question is which side we are on.

Somalia’s Secessionists and the Netanyahu Bet That Backfired

Many Somalis — and many friends of Somalia — were stunned to see secessionist politicians, and some Somalis in northern Somalia (i.e. Somaliland), openly align themselves with Netanyahu, arguably one of the most internationally isolated and discredited leader.

While social media fixated on reactions across Somalia’s political divide, the more consequential question was how this norm-breaking move was interpreted beyond Somalia. That external reaction is where the real story lies.

Supporters of secessionism flooded social media with openly anti-Somalia, anti-Arab and anti-Palestinian rhetoric. Some statements were later walked back, but not before exposing a political project detached from restraint, responsibility, or any serious understanding of statecraft.  By hitching their cause to Netanyahu — a polarizing figure even within Israel — secessionist leaders badly misjudged both their actions and the consequences.

Rather than triggering a cascade of recognitions, the opposite occurred. African states, the Arab and Muslim worlds, European governments committed to international law, and even the United States — whose overriding concerns remain counterterrorism against Al-Shabaab and ISIS operating in Somalia, as well as Red Sea stability — declined to follow Netanyahu’s lead. 

The majority of UN member states openly sided with Somalia; others quietly but firmly distanced themselves from Netanyahu’s actions. Across capitals, the assessment converged: this was a destabilizing risk to peace and stability in the Horn of Africa and beyond.

That conclusion hardened when Israeli disclosures and subsequent reporting suggested that, in exchange for recognition, secessionist actors had entertained proposals involving the relocation of up to 1.5 million Palestinians to northern Somalia and the use of Somali territory as a platform for military operations against Israel’s adversaries, including the Houthis and Iran.

Moreover, states that view the Red Sea as a strategic rear flank — notably Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey — interpreted the move as a direct threat to their own security interests. Diplomatic and security alarms followed.

For the African Union and the UN Security Council, the implications were equally clear. Dismembering Somalia and drawing Israel into the Horn of Africa would not be a localized political matter, but a precedent-setting challenge to African sovereignty and territorial integrity. If Somalia — one of Africa’s most homogeneous countries — could be fractured through opportunism and foreign entanglement, no African state would be immune, the African Union concluded.

All of this unfolded as Netanyahu himself faced deepening global isolation over the war in Gaza and its unprecedented civilian death toll. Yet it was precisely at this moment that secessionist leaders chose to throw their lot in with him — and wrongly assumed that Washington could be pressured or persuaded into recognition. 

What they failed to grasp is that U.S. policy is driven by security interests, not sentiment, and that letting Somalia be and maintaining already tenuous Red Sea stability align far more closely with American interests and strategy than indulging secessionist or Netanyahu-linked adventurism.

Geography also exposes the danger embodied in the separatists’ gamble. Northern Somali cities such as Berbera and Hargeisa lie roughly 600 kilometers from Yemen. Recent wars involving Israel, Iran, and the Houthis have shown how missiles are launched into cities, with civilians paying the price. At that distance, there is little protection: strikes could reach urban centers within minutes. What was sold as leverage has instead exposed civilians to immediate risk.

In short, the secessionist recklessness did not weaken Somalia. It unveiled reality — clarifying the stakes, rallying partners, and exposing the dangers embedded in their miscalculations.

26-kii Diseembar, Israa’iil waxay noqotay dalkii ugu horreeyay ee si rasmi ah u aqoonsada madax-bannaanida Somaliland.
Israa’iil iyo Somaliland waxay kala saxiixdeen heshiis is-aqoonsi iyo xiriir diblomaasiyadeed oo buuxa, oo ay ku jiraan furitaanka safaarado.
27-kii Diseembar, afhayeenka arrimaha dibadda ee Midowga Yurub, Anouar El Anouni, wuxuu sheegay in Midowga Yurub “uu mar kale adkaynayo muhiimadda ay leedahay ilaalinta midnimada, madax-bannaanida iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya.”
6-dii Janaayo, Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda ee Israa’iil Gideon Sa’ar ayaa booqday Somaliland, taasoo noqotay booqashadii ugu horreysay ee rasmi ah oo uu sameeyo hoggaamiye sare oo Israa’iili ah oo tagta Geeska Afrika.
Sa’ar wuxuu booqday Hargeysa, caasimadda Somaliland, isagoo martiqaad ka helay Madaxweynaha Somaliland Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdullaahi.
Taariikhda Somaliland
Somaliland markii ugu horreysay waxay xorriyaddeeda ka qaadatay gumeystihii Ingiriiska sanadkii 1960. Israa’iil waxay ka mid ahayd 35 dal oo aqoonsaday Somaliland xilligaas. Si kastaba, shan maalmood kaddib, Somaliland waxay go’aansatay inay la midoobto dhulkii Talyaanigu gumaysan jiray si loo sameeyo Soomaaliya.
Dagaalladii sokeeye ee 1980-meeyadii kaddib, Somaliland mar kale ayay ku dhawaaqday madax-bannaani sanadkii 1991. Tan iyo markaas waxay u shaqaynaysay dal dhab ah (de facto state), inkastoo aan si ballaaran loo aqoonsan. Aqoonsiga Israa’iil wuxuu ahaa horumar diblomaasiyadeed oo weyn.
Amniga iyo dimuqraadiyadda
Marka loo eego Soomaaliya, oo ay halis ku tahay kooxda argagixisada ah ee Al-Shabaab, Somaliland waa nabad iyo xasillooni. In ka badan 20 sano, waxay lahayd nidaam dimuqraadi ah oo xisbiyo badan leh, doorashooyin joogto ah iyo is-wareejin awood oo nabad ah.
Saaxiibbada ugu dhow ee caalamiga ah waxaa ka mid ah Taiwan iyo Imaaraadka Carabta (UAE).
Muhiimadda istaraatiijiyadeed
Somaliland waxay ku taallaa Gacanka Cadmeed. In ka badan 10% ganacsiga caalamka iyo ku dhowaad saddex meelood meel dhoofinta saliidda ayaa mara marin-biyoodkan. Waxay saamayn ku leedahay marinada Badda Cas, Kanaalka Suweys, iyo dekedda Eilat ee Israa’iil.
Iyadoo maleeshiyaad ay taageerto Iiraan oo ka hawlgala Yemen ay khatar ku yihiin marinada badda, Israa’iil waxay dan weyn ka leedahay inay hesho saaxiibbo lagu kalsoon yahay. Somaliland oo xasilloon waxay gacan ka geysanaysaa ammaanka maraakiibta iyo ka hortagga ballaarinta saameynta Iiraan.
Falcelinta Midowga Yurub
Midowga Yurub wuxuu ku baaqay wadahadal u dhexeeya Somaliland iyo Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya si loo xalliyo khilaafaadka soo jireenka ah.
Laakiin Kayse Maxamed, wariye, falanqeeye iyo diblomaasi ah oo matala Somaliland ee Brussels, ayaa sheegay:
“Midowga Yurub wuxuu ka soo horjeedaa rabitaanka shacabka Somaliland. Waxay aaminsan yihiin inay ku khasbi karaan shacabka Somaliland inay la midoobaan dowlad been ah oo Soomaaliya ka jirta.”
Wuxuu intaa ku daray:
“Siyaasadaha Midowga Yurub waa kuwo duugoobay oo u baahan dib-u-habayn. Somaliland waxay leedahay dood sharci, mid siyaasadeed iyo mid anshaxeed oo ay ku mutaysato aqoonsi.”
Mareykanka ma raaci doonaa Israa’iil?
Kayse Maxamed wuxuu aaminsan yahay in Mareykanku aqoonsan doono Somaliland mustaqbalka dhow. Si kastaba, waxaa jira cadaadis ka imanaya Turkiga, Qatar, Sacuudiga, Jabuuti iyo Shiinaha.
Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda ee Shiinaha Wang Yi ayaa qorsheynayay booqasho Muqdisho ah, balse waa la hakiyay.
Maxamed wuxuu yiri:
“Waxaan u baahanahay Mareykanka inuu na aqoonsado. Dowladda Soomaaliya waxay nagu hanjabtay inay adeegsato awood ciidan. Haddii Mareykanku aqoonsado Somaliland, cidna ma soo weerari doonto.”
Mowqifka Israa’iil
Safiiro Israa’iil u fadhiya Qaramada Midoobay Danny Danon wuxuu ku tilmaamay cambaareynta lagu sameeyay Israa’iil laba-wajiilnimo iyo munaafaqnimo.
Wuxuu yiri:
“Marka dalal si iskood ah u aqoonsadaan Falastiin, wax dhibaato ah lama arko. Laakiin marka Israa’iil aqoonsato Somaliland—dal shaqeynaya oo dimuqraadi ah—golaha ammaanku si degdeg ah ayuu u fadhiistaa.”
Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda ee Israa’iil ayaa sheegay:
“Somaliland ma aha dal muuqaal ah sida Falastiin. Waa dal si buuxda u shaqeeya, dimuqraadi ah muddo ku dhow 35 sano, leh doorashooyin xor ah, saaxiib la ah reer galbeedka, kana saaxiib ah Israa’iil.”
Gunaanad
Mareykanku wuxuu difaacay go’aanka Israa’iil, inkastoo uu caddeeyay inuusan wali beddelin siyaasaddiisa ku aaddan Somaliland.
Madaxweynaha Somaliland ayaa la filayaa inuu booqasho rasmi ah ku tago Israa’iil, iyadoo labada dal ay qorsheynayaan furitaanka safaarado, isla markaana Somaliland ay ku biiri karto Heshiisyada Abraham (Abraham Accords).
Haddii aad rabto soo-koob kooban, falanqayn siyaasadeed, ama qaab war-saxaafadeed Somali ah, ii sheeg.

The group receives direct support from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Quds Force (IRGC-QF), including training, funding, and weapons transfers. • Types and Examples:
• Fixed-wing drones similar to Iranian designs like the Sammad-1 (range up to ~500 km).
• Shahed-101 explosive drones (commonly used in attacks since 2023).

• One-way attack UAVs used in strikes on U.S. facilities, with ranges allowing attacks on bases in Iraq, Syria, Jordan, and even further afield.
• Usage: The group has conducted hundreds of drone attacks as part of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, targeting U.S. positions (e.g., Al-Asad Air Base) and, in some cases, Israel. Drones have been a primary tool since 2020–2021, with increased sophistication mirroring Yemeni Houthi tactics. In 2024–2025 reports, drones were used in attacks on Israel and U.S. targets, including the deadly January 2024 Tower 22 strike in Jordan.
Missile Capabilities (Rockets, Ballistic, and Cruise)Kataib Hezbollah possesses a range of rockets and missiles, many supplied by Iran since at least 2018. These include short-range ballistic missiles (SRBMs) and indications of cruise missile use.
• Rockets and Short-Range Ballistic Missiles:
• Rockets (various calibers) for indirect fire attacks.
• SRBMs: Fateh-110 (range ~250–300 km), Zolfaghar (range ~700 km), and Zelzal variants. These could reach U.S. bases in Iraq or, from western Iraq, potentially Israel.
• Precision-guided or tactical missiles mentioned in group statements.
• Cruise Missiles:
• Evidence points to use of advanced cruise missiles, such as Iranian Paveh derivatives (e.g., Arqab or Quds-class, range ~1,000+ km).
• In 2025 interviews and claims, spokesmen referenced "advanced cruise missiles" in attacks on Israel, launched from areas like Babil, Karbala, and Anbar.
• Failed launches (e.g., Quds-class in Babil) and claims of using them against regional targets highlight this capability, though less frequent than drones or rockets.
The militia has paraded or displayed systems like anti-aircraft missiles, armed vehicles, and precision weapons. It controls key PMF (Popular Mobilization Forces) departments related to missiles and anti-armor. Overall Assessment Kataib Hezbollah's arsenal emphasizes asymmetric warfare: inexpensive, hard-to-trace drones for harassment and precision strikes, supplemented by Iranian-supplied missiles for escalation. Capabilities have grown since 2018, with transfers of SRBMs and drone tech. While not as vast as Lebanese Hezbollah's rocket arsenal, it poses significant threats to U.S. forces in the region and contributes to long-range attacks on Israel via the Islamic Resistance umbrella. These assessments draw from open-source analyses by think tanks like the Washington Institute, CSIS Missile Threat Project, and Long War Journal, as well as U.S. government designations. 13 JAN 2026 IRAQI Kataib Hezbollah Drone Tactics 
 as a key component of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq (IRI), employs drone tactics that show clear parallels to those of the Houthis (Ansar Allah) in Yemen, largely due to shared Iranian support from the IRGC-Quds Force. Both groups rely on Iranian-supplied or reverse-engineered drone designs for asymmetric, low-cost attacks that prioritize harassment, propaganda, and limited escalation while avoiding direct confrontation with superior air defenses. Similarities in Drone Tactics
• Shared Technology and Designs: Both use Iranian-origin one-way attack (kamikaze) drones, such as variants of the Ababil series (e.g., Ababil-T/Qasef-1 for Houthis, Basir-1 for KH) and Sammad family (Sammad-1/3 used by Houthis and similar fixed-wing models by Iraqi militias). These enable ranges from hundreds to over 1,000 km, allowing strikes on distant targets like U.S. bases, Saudi facilities (historically for Houthis), or Israel.
• Kamikaze/Explosive Payload Focus: Tactics emphasize pilot-to-target (suicide) strikes where drones crash into or near targets and detonate. This mirrors Houthi "pilot-to-target" attacks on shipping or bases, differing from more complex loitering or swarming seen elsewhere.
• Propaganda and Headline-Grabbing: Attacks often aim more at media impact and psychological pressure than massive destruction, given small payloads and limited accuracy. Houthis have used this for years against Saudi Arabia/Riyadh (e.g., headline-focused penetrations), while KH/IRI does the same against U.S. positions and Israel.
• Asymmetric Harassment and Escalation Control: Both launch frequent, low-intensity strikes to wear down defenses, force resource allocation, and signal solidarity (e.g., with Palestinians post-October 2023). They adapt to countermeasures, like timing attacks during U.S. drone returns (Tower 22 incident) or exploiting gaps.
• Joint/Collaborative Operations: Evidence of coordination exists, including joint claims with Houthis on Israel strikes (e.g., 2024 Haifa/Eilat claims), shared expertise (Hezbollah mentoring both on drones), and even personnel exchanges (e.g., Houthi drone specialist killed at KH site).
Key Differences in Drone Tactics
• Scale and Frequency: Houthis have conducted far more sustained, high-volume operations, especially in the Red Sea (hundreds of attacks on shipping since late 2023, including combined drone/missile barrages, explosive unmanned surface vessels, and swarms). KH/IRI focuses on dozens to hundreds of attacks, mostly against U.S. bases in Iraq/Syria/Jordan and occasional long-range ones on Israel, but not at the same maritime disruption scale.
• Target Set and Strategic Goals: Houthis prioritize naval/maritime interdiction (Red Sea/Gulf of Aden shipping to pressure Israel-linked trade, causing global rerouting and economic impact) alongside land strikes on Israel/Saudi. KH targets land-based U.S./coalition forces (e.g., Al-Asad, Tower 22 deadly strike) and Israel from Iraq/Syria, aiming to expel U.S. presence and support "Axis of Resistance."
• Innovation and Adaptation: Houthis have matured faster in long-range strikes (e.g., modified Sammad-3 reaching Tel Aviv in 2024) and combined arms (drones + ballistic/cruise missiles + USVs). KH shows sophistication (e.g., precision timing, adapting to defenses) but remains more localized, with less emphasis on swarms or naval elements.
• Defensive Environment: Houthis face intense U.S./UK/coalition strikes degrading capabilities (e.g., 2024-2025 airstrikes reducing missile/drone fires), yet persist. KH operates in a more permissive Iraqi environment (PMF integration) but faces U.S. retaliatory strikes on drone sites.
Overall, KH's tactics appear to draw inspiration from—and in some cases directly mirror—the Houthi model of persistent, low-cost drone warfare for political leverage and propaganda. Both exemplify Iran's proxy strategy: export affordable, deniable tech to create multi-front pressure without direct IRGC involvement. However, Houthis have scaled this into a broader maritime/economic disruption campaign, while KH remains more focused on land/U.S.-centric harassment in the Iraq-Syria theater. Capabilities continue evolving with Iranian tech transfers, as seen in joint operations and shared designs.
The Ababil (Persian for "Swallow") is a family of Iranian tactical unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) developed by the Iran Aircraft Manufacturing Industrial Company (HESA) since the 1980s. It is a low-cost, multirole platform emphasizing asymmetric warfare, with variants serving reconnaissance, surveillance, target drone training, and one-way attack (kamikaze/loitering munition) roles. The family is widely proliferated to Iranian proxies, including Hezbollah (as Mirsad), Houthis in Yemen (as Qasef series), and Kataib Hezbollah in Iraq (as Basir-1).Key characteristics across most variants include pusher-propeller configuration, fiberglass/composite construction for low radar signature, catapult or rocket-assisted launch (no runway needed), and ranges typically 100–200+ km. Early models were rudimentary, but later ones added precision guidance, night capabilities, and arming options.Main Variants and Details
• Ababil-1 (1980s prototype/pre-production)
An obscure early loitering munition/suicide drone with ~40 kg explosive payload. Little documentation exists—no known photos, combat use, or current service. Considered a developmental step toward Ababil-2.
• Ababil-2 (1990s, most common base model)
Delta-wing/canard design, reusable target drone with basic surveillance. Endurance: 1.25–2 hours. Range: ~100 km. Speed: up to 370 km/h (dive). Ceiling: ~3,350 m.
Variants/sub-designations: 
• Ababil-B/S/R: Target/surveillance focus (acoustic miss-distance indicators, IR devices, radar reflectors). 
• Ababil-T (twin-tail short/medium-range attack variant): Often the export/strike version. Payload: up to 40 kg warhead or surveillance gear. This is the primary kamikaze base for proxies. 
• Houthi: Rebranded as Qasef-1 (since ~2016, explosive charge/warhead for strikes on Saudi/UAE targets; disputed local production but Iranian-sourced). 
• Hezbollah: Mirsad-1. 
• Kataib Hezbollah: Related designs.
• Qasef-2K (Houthi evolution of Ababil-T/Qasef-1): Airburst at ~20 m altitude for shrapnel effect (used in attacks like Al Anad Air Base, killing personnel). Warhead ~30 kg.
• Ababil-3 (2000s, larger ISR-focused upgrade)
Twin-boom design (similar to South African Denel Seeker influence), improved surveillance (rotating cameras, night vision since 2014). Endurance: up to 4–8 hours. Range: ~100–200 km roundtrip. Speed: ~200 km/h. Ceiling: ~5,000 m.
Armable in later versions (e.g., with Ghaem/Qaem bombs). 
• Kataib Hezbollah: Rebranded as Basir-1 (used for spying, e.g., over Tikrit vs. ISIS). 
• Operators: IRGC, exported to Sudan (as Zagil III-B), Syria, Iraq PMF militias.
• Ababil-4 (revealed ~2022, limited info)
Further evolution with longer range/endurance than Ababil-3. Used in reconnaissance, surveillance, or combat. Seen in Iranian military parades/exercises but sparse details.
• Ababil-5 (unveiled 2022, most advanced)
UCAV hybrid (recon + combat), blending Ababil-3/Mohajer-6 features. Length: 8 m. Wingspan: ~12 m. Range: up to 2,400 km (claimed). Endurance: 12–24 hours. Ceiling: 7,000 m. Speed: ~210 km/h. MTOW: ~1,000 kg. Payload: up to 150 kg (e.g., 4 Almas anti-tank missiles ~10 km range, or 6 Qaem-1/4 Qaem-5 precision bombs ~40 km). Engine: Rotax 915 clone (141 hp). Reduced RCS nose design. Demonstrated in Iranian Army exercises (2024).
Proxy Adaptations and UsageIran exports designs/components for local assembly/modification, enabling deniable proliferation. 
• Houthis: Primarily Ababil-2/T-based (Qasef-1/2K) for early attacks on Saudi radar/bases; supplemented by longer-range Samad family. 
• Hezbollah: Ababil-2/T (Mirsad-1) for strikes on Israel (e.g., downing assets, base attacks). 
• Kataib Hezbollah: Ababil-3 (Basir-1) for ISR/attacks on U.S. forces.
The Ababil family's evolution reflects Iran's focus on affordable, exportable tech for proxy warfare—persistent harassment via low-cost kamikaze drones, with growing precision and range in newer models. Exact specs vary by source/modifications, and inventories remain opaque due to clandestine transfers.

l’annulation de l’ensemble des accords conclus avec les Émirats arabes unis (#EAU), y compris les accords bilatéraux de coopération en matière de sécurité et de défense.

Cette décision intervient dans un contexte de tensions liées à la reconnaissance par Israël de l’indépendance du Somaliland, territoire séparatiste dont Mogadiscio revendique la souveraineté.

Dans une déclaration officielle, le gouvernement somalien précise que tous les accords impliquant les institutions fédérales, les entités affiliées et les administrations régionales opérant sur le territoire somalien sont annulés. La décision fait suite à des rapports crédibles et à des preuves convaincantes d’actions hostiles portant atteinte à la souveraineté nationale, à l’unité territoriale et à l’indépendance politique du pays.

Sont notamment concernés les ports de Berbera (au Somaliland), de Bosaso (au Puntland, nord-est) et de Kismayo (au Jubaland, sud-ouest), ainsi que les accords passés avec les administrations régionales. Les Émirats arabes unis sont également soupçonnés d’avoir facilité la fuite du chef des séparatistes yéménites vers Abou Dhabi en utilisant des ports somaliens, ce qui a conduit les autorités locales à ouvrir une enquête sur l’usage présumé non autorisé de l’espace aérien et des infrastructures nationales.

Le Somaliland, situé au nord-ouest de la Somalie et représentant plus d’un quart du territoire que revendique Mogadiscio, s’est autoproclamé république indépendante en 1991. Depuis, il fonctionne en autonomie, avec sa propre monnaie, son armée et sa police, et bénéficie d’une relative stabilité par rapport à la Somalie, marquée par l’insurrection islamiste des shebab et les conflits politiques récurrents. Sa position stratégique sur le détroit de Bab-el-Mandeb, qui relie la mer Rouge au golfe d’Aden, renforce l’importance géopolitique de ce territoire.

La décision israélienne de reconnaître le Somaliland comme État indépendant, le 26 décembre dernier, a été perçue par le président somalien Hassan Sheikh Mohamud comme une « menace » pour la sécurité et la stabilité de la Corne de l’Afrique. Les Émirats arabes unis, qui n’ont pas condamné cette reconnaissance contrairement à l’Arabie saoudite, sont soupçonnés d’avoir soutenu cette initiative.

Le gouvernement somalien a indiqué que cette décision ne remettait pas en cause sa volonté de coopération internationale, à condition qu’elle repose sur le respect mutuel, la reconnaissance de l’unité et de la souveraineté de la Somalie, ainsi que sur le respect des principes constitutionnels et du droit international. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères a été chargé de notifier officiellement les Émirats arabes unis et de coordonner la mise en œuvre de cette décision, tout en informant les partenaires internationaux et régionaux.

SHOULD HE STAY OR SHOULD HE GO?
✍️ Ben Thirkell

After Robin Roefs saved the third penalty on Saturday it was, as always seems to be the case when we have been in a shootout over the last seven or so years, Luke O’Nien to step up next.

In a week dominated by Enzo Le Fee’s penalty at Brentford, the Frenchman had already redeemed himself and up against England number one and boyhood Mackem Jordan Pickford, O’Nien ran up and absolutely belted it past him, no silly run up, no messing around and booked our place in the next round.

Although Roefs was very much the hero, it felt almost poetic that it was Luke to score the deciding penalty, a man who is one of few who has been through it all with us fans: from play-off heartbreak, back-to-back first-round FA Cup exits at the hands of Mansfield, to winning twice at Wembley and knocking Everton out of said cup with Granit Xhaka as a teammate. It has been a wild ride and O’Nien has been in the front seat throughout.

With just three Premier League appearances to his name this campaign, all off the bench for a total of 10 minutes and one red card, opportunities have understandably been limited with recruitment heavily focused on the backline during the summer, which so far has worked extremely well. There were some suggestions that O’Nien’s winning penalty could possibly be his last moment in red and white, with links to Championship clubs and our rumoured interest in Jhon Lucumi (which is now believed to have ended with the defender out injured for the next month). However, on Saturday LO9 made it perfectly clear in his post-match interview that he does not want to leave the club and is adamant on staying at SAFC regardless of limited opportunities to play. I actually think he’d pay the club to let him stay, if it came down to that!

It is a strange time for O’Nien as he proved on Saturday he is absolutely still a useful option for the club. But, with the quality we have brought in, you still struggle to see how he would get into the side and in theory a temporary move to a play-off-chasing Championship side would make sense. However, what O’Nien brings to the side off the pitch is very clearly important. After the derby win it emerged that he was the one to give the pre-match team talk instead of Xhaka.

There is a section of our fanbase that for some reason aren’t fond of O’Nien, but I feel although he has his moments, he was one of our best players last year and that has been the case throughout his time at Sunderland, whether it be centre-back, right-back, centre-midfield or even playing just behind the striker, he has constantly given his all and performed in a Sunderland shirt. For me, if O’Nien is happy to play a smaller role on the pitch then I think it is ideal to keep him around purely for his impact off it.

He loves it here and although at the age of 31, most would maybe want to go and play regularly, as he always has since joining, he will want to prove any doubters wrong and show he can be more than capable at this level and you have to respect that.

I saw a quote the other day and it couldn’t be more true: without Luke O’Nien, there’s no Granit Xhaka. It will be a sad day when the inevitable happens and he does move on or retire but for now, he seems to be sticking around, and I am sure a good portion of the fanbase are more than happy with that. He’ll be a great coach one day!
