Globalisation in action

THE phenomenon (رجحان / مظہر) of globalisation (عالمگیریت) began after industrialisation (صنعت کاری).

This technology has helped connect the world in social, economic, and political dimensions (ابعاد). People-to-people connections were established (قائم کی گئیں) to share knowledge (علم) and experience (تجربہ). Institutions (ادارے) started collaborating (تعاون کرنا) in their areas of interest (دلچسپی), and states came together for mutual benefits (باہمی فوائد). During industrialization, the West imported skilled workers (ماہر کارکن) from developing countries for its markets, and this trend (رجحان) continued with technology-driven businesses. In real spirit (حقیقی روح میں), globalization promised trade, ideas, technology, and inclusion (شمولیت) in a “global village.” Pakistan, like many other countries, embraced (قبول کیا) this promise. However, millions of young people today suggest a different story, that is, globalization is not only about markets and mobility (نقل و حرکت). It also involves attention (توجہ), influence (اثر), and control (کنٹرول). The new contest (مقابلہ) is not merely over territory (علاقہ) or tariffs (محصولات). It is over the most valuable commodity (قیمتی اثاثہ) of the digital age, human time.

According to the World Bank, Pakistan’s population is approximately (تقریباً) 251 million, making it one of the most populous (گنجان آبادی والا) countries in the world. The UNDP states that approximately 65% of the population is youth. The question arises (سوال پیدا ہوتا ہے) whether the youth are being given the opportunity of education and properly engaged (شامل) in socio-economic development (سماجی و معاشی ترقی) or are being quietly diverted (بھٹکایا جا رہا ہے). Although access (رسائی) to higher education has increased from 2.5% in 2002 to around 13% in 2024, much remains to be done to engage these bright minds in the development of the country. The PTA figures show an increase in smartphone users as well as high-speed internet in the country, which is good for offering programs, diplomas, and certificates in high-demand (زیادہ طلب والے) disciplines (شعبے). Smartphones have become essential (ضروری) for business and communication. Similarly, these can be a better platform for learning management systems, where books, activities, interactions (تبادلہ), and assessments (جائزہ) can be carried out for effective learning. However, it is observed that users are mostly addicted (عادی) to reels and other social media content, which just consumes (ضائع کرتا ہے) their time to benefit those who have created content.

Our youth are exposed (سامنا ہے) to boundary-less (بے حد و سرحد) social media where they live inside algorithmic (الگورتھم پر مبنی) ecosystems (نظام), and these platforms set the tempo (رفتار) of aspiration (خواہش), anxiety (بے چینی), entertainment (تفریح), outrage (غصہ), and consumption (استعمال). Social media platforms are developed to capture the attention of users and maximize (زیادہ سے زیادہ کرنا) profits (منافع) by engaging them with content they like, thereby generating revenue (آمدنی) and market influence. These platforms are developed to optimize (بہتر بنانا) attention and interaction. These videos are designed to trigger (ابھارنا) strong emotions, quick reactions, and repetitive (بار بار) viewing. They engage users through infinite scrolling (لامحدود اسکرولنگ), autoplay (خودکار چلنا), push notifications (اطلاعات), and short video loops. As a result, users remain online longer than intended (ارادہ), often by exploiting (استحصال) predictable (قابلِ پیش گوئی) human vulnerabilities (کمزوریاں).

This has created a new type of profession (پیشہ) called an influencer, who continuously (مسلسل) engages users with content that is liked and shared by them. They try to increase subscriptions (سبسکرپشنز) and viewership (ناظرین) for monetization (کمائی). They show and sell their lifestyle (طرزِ زندگی) but not their livelihood (روزگار) to users. Users are following trends and missing training for their livelihoods. This creates a dangerous illusion (وہم) of online fame that is real for a few days, months or years. There is no real impact (اثر) on societal development (معاشرتی ترقی) and growth. This trend of social attention is developing a nation of content consumers rather than content creators. By following viral content, social media users are silently trained as consumers of these platforms.

Every user activity on social media platforms generates data (ڈیٹا), which are used for prediction (پیش گوئی), and prediction generates profit and power for social media platforms that are usually not in our country. Moreover, these social media platforms are not always accountable (جوابدہ) for violations (خلاف ورزی) of our religious, local values, and ethics (اخلاقیات). A major reason why we are exposed to social media is that it provides relief (راحت) from various social problems, such as unemployment (بیروزگاری) and limited growth opportunities. There are verified (تصدیق شدہ) projects that were carried out during the war on terror, wherein the youth in the FATA region were engaged in social media apps with some rewards (انعامات) to experiment (تجربہ) whether their attention can be diverted or not. The experiment worked well, and that pilot experiment (ابتدائی تجربہ) is now an open secret (کھلا راز) for companies to engage youth in the developing world as their respondents (جواب دہندگان).

Pakistan can develop a national strategy (قومی حکمتِ عملی) to educate and engage its youth. They can be engaged in learning new skills and training in demanding skills. They should be trained to follow trainers rather than influencers. We need to engage them in activities that are good for the development of society and the country. Institutions in the country must develop a system of supervised (نگرانی شدہ) teaching and learning, which can help engage youth in schools, colleges, and universities. There must also be opportunities for engagement after graduation; otherwise, global influencers will engage them in non-productive (غیر پیداواری) viewership videos, reels, and similar content. There are many success stories of countries like China, Malaysia, and Korea, which have converted their potential (صلاحیت) into profitable (منافع بخش) products. If they are not engaged constructively (تعمیری طور پر), non-state actors can engage them; we would be silent viewers watching how global eyes are in action for their benefit.

— The writer is Director, Higher Education Commission, Islamabad.

Muneer Ahmed Mirjat

Chapter 1: The Content Vultures

The gravel of the parking lot bit into Lily’s knees, sharp and unforgiving. It was a cold Tuesday in Oakhaven, Ohio the kind of day where the wind tasted like wet iron and broken dreams.

Lily didn't mind the cold. She was used to it. She was used to the grease stains on her apron from a double shift at The Rusty Hub, and she was used to the way people looked through her, as if she were made of glass.

But she wasn't used to this.

"C'mon, Lily-poo! Don't look so sad. Think of the engagement!"

Jax Miller held his iPhone less than six inches from her face. He was twenty-two, smelled of expensive cologne and entitlement, and had three million followers who thrived on watching him humiliate "the little people." To Jax, the world wasn't a place to live in; it was a stage, and everyone else was just an unpaid extra.

Beside him, Lexi, his girlfriend and primary camera operator, adjusted the lighting ring. "The shadows are hitting her eyes perfectly, babe. She looks totally devastated. Keep going."

Lily tried to stand up, her hands clutching the brown paper bag containing her only meal for the day a bruised apple and some leftover fries. Jax shoved her back down. It wasn't a violent shove, just firm enough to keep her grounded. Firm enough to show her he owned the space she occupied.

"Please," Lily whispered, her voice cracking. "I just want to catch the bus. My shift starts in twenty minutes."

"The bus can wait. The internet can't," Jax grinned, his teeth unnaturally white. "Now, do the thing. Look into the lens and tell my subscribers what it’s like to be totally alone in the world. Tell them how it feels to have no mom, no dad, and nobody coming to save you."

A small crowd had gathered. This was Oakhaven a town where the biggest news was usually a sale at the hardware store. Seeing a "famous" YouTuber in the wild was an event. They stood in a semi-circle, a wall of glowing screens, capturing Lily’s shame from every angle.

No one stepped forward.

"I have people," Lily said, her voice small but steady.

Lexi laughed, a sharp, metallic sound. "Honey, we did our research. You’ve been bouncing around foster homes since you were six. Your file is a graveyard. You’re the definition of 'nobody.'"

Jax leaned in, dropping his voice to a mock-sympathetic whisper. "Just say it, Lily. Say: 'I'm a nobody and I'm begging for your likes.' If you do, I’ll give you a hundred dollars. That’s more than you make in a week at that greasy spoon, right?"

He reached into his pocket and pulled out a crisp hundred-dollar bill, dangling it like a carrot in front of a starving horse.

Lily looked at the bill. Then she looked at the faces in the crowd. She saw a middle-aged woman she recognized from the diner Mrs. Higgins. Mrs. Higgins usually tipped her fifty cents and asked about her day. Now, Mrs. Higgins was holding her phone up, her eyes wide with a disturbing kind of hunger.

Lily felt a coldness spreading from her chest to her limbs. It wasn't the weather. It was the realization that to these people, she wasn't a human being. She was a "moment." She was "content."

"No," Lily said.

Jax’s grin flickered. "What was that?"

"I said no. Keep your money."

She tried to crawl away, but Lexi stepped on the hem of her long, faded skirt. The fabric tore with a sickening rip.

"Oops," Lexi smirked. "Guess you’re staying a little longer."

Jax’s face hardened. The "nice guy" persona he used for his 'Kindness Prank' videos evaporated. He grabbed the bottle of chilled Fiji water from Lexi’s hand.

"You know, Lily, the algorithm loves a transformation," Jax said. He unscrewed the cap. "Let's see how you look with a little 'baptism.'"

He began to pour the water slowly over her head. The icy liquid soaked through her thin hair, ran down her neck, and turned her cheap uniform transparent. The crowd gasped, but the phones stayed up.

"There she is!" Jax shouted to the camera. "The face of Oakhaven! Give us a sob, Lily! Give us those tears!"

Lily didn't cry. She closed her eyes, her breath coming in ragged gasps. She reached into the pocket of her apron and felt the small, heavy object hidden there. A heavy brass coin. On one side was an eagle. On the other, the words: Respect All, Fear None.

It was a gift from a man she called "Uncle Bear."

"You shouldn't have done that," Lily whispered, her eyes still shut.

"Oh yeah? And who's gonna stop me?" Jax laughed, turning to the crowd. "Who's gonna stop me from making this girl a star?"

As if in answer, a low, tectonic thrum began to vibrate through the pavement. It was faint at first a hum you felt in your teeth more than you heard in your ears.

Jax frowned, looking around. "Is that an earthquake?"

The sound grew. It wasn't a hum anymore. It was a roar. A rhythmic, mechanical growl that sounded like a thousand lions waking up at once. It was the sound of internal combustion and unbridled power.

At the edge of the parking lot, the first one appeared.

A massive black Harley-Davidson Road Glide, its chrome screaming in the sunlight. The rider was a giant of a man, wearing a leather vest with a patch that sent a shiver through every local who saw it: Iron Brotherhood - Original Member.

Behind him came another. And another. And ten more. Then fifty.

They didn't just drive in; they invaded. They moved in a perfect, terrifying formation, the sound of 500 engines drowning out Jax’s voice, the wind from their passage blowing the hats off the spectators.

The bikers circled the area, trapping the crowd, the influencers, and Lily in a ring of steel and thunder. The smell of gasoline and hot asphalt filled the air.

The lead biker the giant kicked his stand down. The engine died with a final, menacing cough. He dismounted, his boots heavy on the gravel. He was six-foot-five, with a grey-streaked beard that reached his chest and arms the size of tree trunks, covered in faded war tattoos.

He didn't look at the crowd. He didn't look at Jax, who had turned a sickly shade of grey and lowered his phone.

The giant walked straight to Lily.

He looked at her wet hair, her torn skirt, and the spilled fries on the ground. His eyes, blue and sharp as daggers, turned to ice.

"Lily-bug," the man said, his voice a low rumble that seemed to shake the very air. "You didn't call the clubhouse."

Lily looked up, a single tear finally escaping. "I didn't want to bother you, Bear. You were in the middle of the Memorial Run."

Bear reached out a massive, calloused hand and gently wiped the tear from her cheek. Then he stood up, turning his gaze toward Jax.

Jax took a step back, nearly tripping over his own tripod. "Hey, man... we’re just... we’re just filming a video. It’s a prank! There’s cameras everywhere! We’re making her famous!"

Bear didn't say a word. He just raised a hand.

Five hundred bikers dismounted in unison. The sound of 500 kickstands hitting the ground was like a gavel striking a death sentence.

They didn't look like "content creators." They looked like an army. And they were looking at Jax like he was something they’d found on the bottom of their boots.

"You like cameras, kid?" Bear asked, his voice terrifyingly calm.

Jax nodded weakly, his iPhone trembling in his hand.

"Good," Bear said, stepping into Jax’s personal space until the influencer had to crane his neck back to see the biker's face. "Because we’re gonna give you the most viral afternoon of your life."

Bear looked over his shoulder. "Boys! Get the livestream going. The world needs to see what happens when you mess with the Brotherhood’s daughter."

The "nobody" girl wasn't a nobody anymore. She was the most protected person in the state of Ohio. And the vultures were about to find out they were at the bottom of the food chain.

Tax : Facts over fear.

The lifeblood of any modern economy is not just the revenue it generates, but the trust its citizens place in the systems that govern them. When that trust is eroded by a vacuum of information, the consequences are swift, silent, and potentially devastating. Recently, a story emerged from the Nigerian diaspora that serves as a chilling cautionary tale for our economic stability. A female car dealer, an investor bringing hard-earned capital back to her homeland, almost became a casualty of the digital information war. Misled by a pseudo-tax consultant on TikTok, she was convinced that the new Nigeria Tax Act 2025 would see twenty percent of every single bank transaction snatched away by the government.

Panic is a powerful motivator. In a matter of days, this entrepreneur began the frantic process of converting over two hundred million naira of business capital into dollars. Her plan was simple but tragic: shut down her operations, liquidate her assets, and move her investment to another African country where she felt her capital would be safe from "predatory" policies. It was only through a stroke of luck and the intervention of professional guidance that she was shown the reality of the law—that the new Act actually offers significant exemptions for small and medium-sized businesses rather than the blanket theft she had been led to fear. While she rescinded her decision and is now actively advising her fellow diasporans to reconsider their exit plans, the near-miss should send a shudder through the halls of power in Abuja.

This incident is a symptom of a much larger malady: the information gap. When the government fails to speak clearly and loudly to the public, the void is filled by the cacophony of social media "experts" and opportunistic alarmists. If that lady had left, the impact would have been multifaceted and deeply felt. Beyond the immediate loss of two hundred million naira in local circulation, there would have been a ripple effect of job losses for her staff, a dip in government revenue that she would have legitimately paid through other channels, and a significant stain on Nigeria’s reputation as a destination for Foreign Direct Investment. Every time a member of the diaspora pulls out of the country due to a misunderstanding, it sends a signal to the rest of the world that Nigeria is a high-risk, unpredictable terrain. This is a price our fragile economy cannot afford to pay.

 

This incident proves that this is the time for the government to invest heavily in the orientation of the Nigerian tax-paying public. A law is only as good as the public’s understanding of it. If the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 is indeed designed to simplify compliance, eliminate the "2/3rd" restriction for manufacturers, and exempt small businesses with low turnover from corporate tax, then these benefits should be the loudest songs in the media. Instead, we have allowed the narrative to be hijacked by social media content creators who are not only unknowledgeable about the technicalities of taxation but are often motivated by the "clout" of sensationalism. Taxation is a complex, technical field; leaving its explanation to the whims of influencers is a recipe for national economic sabotage.

This task is too monumental to be left in the hands of a single individual or a single agency. While the leadership of the revenue services may be competent, the scale of the challenge requires a multi-agency, "all-hands-on-deck" approach. It is not just about technical tax talk; it is about national orientation. We need the Ministry of Finance, the National Orientation Agency, the Ministry of Information, and the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission to collaborate on a unified narrative. The message must be broken down into local languages, simplified into digestible social media content, and broadcasted through every available channel to reach the market woman in Onitsha, the tech developer in Lagos, and the car dealer in the diaspora.

Proper communication builds the bridge that allows citizens to see tax not as a burden, but as a contribution to the infrastructure and security they so desperately desire. If the government fails to invest heavily in this orientation today, it will spend much more tomorrow trying to repair the damage of a fleeing investor class and an alienated public. The story of the car dealer was a warning shot; let us hope the government hears it before more businesses choose to cross the border into the waiting arms of our neighbours.

WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump's administration has made good on its pledge to label three Middle Eastern branches of the Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist organizations, imposing sanctions on them and their members in a decision that could have implications for U.S. relationships with allies in the region.

The Treasury and State departments announced the actions Tuesday against the Lebanese, Jordanian and Egyptian chapters of the Muslim Brotherhood, which they said pose a risk to the United States and American interests.

The State Department designated the Lebanese branch a foreign terrorist organization, the most severe of the labels, which makes it a criminal offense to provide material support to the group. The Jordanian and Egyptian branches were listed by Treasury as specially designated global terrorists for providing support to Hamas.

“These designations reflect the opening actions of an ongoing, sustained effort to thwart Muslim Brotherhood chapters’ violence and destabilization wherever it occurs,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement. “The United States will use all available tools to deprive these Muslim Brotherhood chapters of the resources to engage in or support terrorism.”

Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were mandated last year under an executive order signed by Trump to determine the most appropriate way to impose sanctions on the groups, which U.S. officials say engage in or support violence and destabilization campaigns that harm the United States and other regions.

“The Muslim Brotherhood has inspired, nurtured, and funded terrorist groups like Hamas, that are direct threats to the safety and security of the American people and our allies,” John Hurley, Treasury undersecretary for terrorism and financial intelligence, said in a statement.

Muslim Brotherhood leaders have said they renounce violence.

Trump's executive order had singled out the chapters in Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt, noting that a wing of the Lebanese chapter had launched rockets on Israel after Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack in Israel that set off the war in Gaza. Leaders of the group in Jordan have provided support to Hamas, the order said.

The Muslim Brotherhood was founded in Egypt in 1928 but was banned in that country in 2013. Jordan announced a sweeping ban on the Muslim Brotherhood in April.

Nathan Brown, a professor of political science and international affairs at George Washington University, said some allies of the U.S., including the United Arab Emirates and Egypt, would likely be pleased with the designation.

“For other governments where the brotherhood is tolerated, it would be a thorn in bilateral relations,” including in Qatar and Turkey, he said. While the Turkish ruling party has been associated with members of the Muslim Brotherhood in the past, the government of Qatar has denied any relationship with it.

Brown also said a designation on the chapters may have effects on visa and asylum claims for people entering not just the U.S. but also Western European countries and Canada.

“I think this would give immigration officials a stronger basis for suspicion, and it might make courts less likely to question any kind of official action against Brotherhood members who are seeking to stay in this country, seeking political asylum,” he said.

Trump, a Republican, weighed whether to designate the Muslim Brotherhood a terrorist organization in 2019 during his first term in office. Some prominent Trump supporters, including right-wing influencer Laura Loomer, have pushed his administration to take aggressive action against the group.

Two Republican-led state governments — Florida and Texas — designated the group as a terrorist organization this year.

The last few months, young men who follow me on social media have started asking me an interesting question: 

“What’s wrong with fascism, anyway?”

This surprised me at first, until I learned quite a lot of modern Influencers and political figures (like Nick Fuentes) have begun to embrace the label and advocate for it. 

It’s something I’d studied in school, and been reading deeply on lately, so ’d like to offer a calm, non-judgmental, non-accusatory academic discussion about what fascism actually is and why it is generally considered a very bad political and governing philosophy. (BTW, it is a political and governing philosophy, not a type of government or economic system.) And I’d like to non-judgmentally discuss the topic with anyone who is curious about it and trying to understand. 

To start with , what is it? Fascism is often used as a slur, which means everyone tries to define it in such a way that it applies to those they disagree with. That way they can use it as a cudgel! (Usually against conservatives.)

So serious non-partisan scholars point out that the important defining things are the things that made it bad, right? For example, fascists are always patriotic, but being patriotic alone isn’t bad or destructive. So if we define “fascism” as “patriotism” we’ve missed the whole point of why fascism is bad. 

The scholars (like Adorno, Arendt, Eco, etc.) teach us that core traits shared by all fascist movements that actually make them bad are:

1. A strong belief in hierarchies—of class, gender, national identity, religion, etc. Some people are more deserving of rights, power, and resources than others. Strong hierarchies bring peace, harmony, and prosperity and make nations great. There’s always a mythology that hierarchies were natural and even “sacred” in the past, and once made a nation great, but were lost, leading to chaos, weakness, and decline. 

2. Violence and force are justified to establish hierarchies, and “might makes right.” Violence, conquest, and dominance aren’t just necessary, but celebrated. 

3. Since might makes right, democracy stands in the way, and only a strong man leader can bring a return to greatness. Over time, the belief in the strong man leader becomes a “fusion” of personality, making fascism a sort of cult of personality. 

And these three things are the firm, clear dividing line scholars use to tell “fascism” from “conservativism.” 

Almost everyone finds hierarchies distasteful AND almost everyone believes in some degree of hierarchy—for example between parents and children or teachers and students. 

Classic Burkean “Conservatives” acknowledge unfair hierarchies are distasteful, but believe in TOLERATING some hierarchies for the purpose of meritocracy, order, social harmony, rule of law, competition, and incentive. 

This belief in harmony, etc. means that conservatives believe strongly in the institutions of republican democracy (even in losing!), fairness, rule of law, and importantly, pluralism—the idea that even when we disagree, we’re one people, due respect and brotherhood. And democracy and fairness are more important than “winning.” 

In my humble opinion, while conservatives may slow down “progress,” this philosophy of conservativism is very natural and helpful in any society. 

This is where we see the clear line between conservativism and fascism: fascism believes in winning at all costs, might is right, and anyone who stands in the way is an “enemy“ to be crushed.

Because ”might makes right” violates some of our most basic shared human values across cultures, scholars agree there’s one clear “entry point to fascism:” called moral inversion. 

Moral inversion is where “rules given by the hierarchy take the place of moral judgement.” (Adorno) And “protesting or resisting injustice becomes more offensive than injustice.” To prepare the way for moral inversion, fascist movements ALWAYS teach to celebrate injustice, shocking jokes, cruelty, and meanness—that might makes right. Fascism actually thrives on the thrill of subverting conventional morality, saying shocking cruel, things. 

This is of course, the antithesis of conservativism‘s appeal to decency, right, and shared morality. 

And since it believes in might making right, and that rules don’t apply, and in hierarchies of oppression, fascism ALWAYS snowballs out of control. This is a defining feature. 

A society can’t microdose fascism. 

Once the line is crossed, such a philosophy makes its own enemies—because nobody wants to live at the bottom of a hierarchy, and a “might makes right” justifies the other side to act violently, too. 

Expansionism and war always become required to unite the hierarchy and deliver on the promise of “greatness.” Rising resistance always leads to greater and greater repression and violence at home. Fear, meanness, and immorality grow. The economies and culture always stagnate and decline for reasons we’ll discuss next time. Since hierarchies are sacred and give law, corruption abounds.

Fascist societies, just like authoritarian communist ones, are terrible places to live for everyone but the rich elite. And so we see why virtually all of our literature, all our movies portray fascistic attitudes as the villains. 

(Picture, Franco’s secret police beating and arresting civilian protestors in Spain.)

WHAT DID TRUMP DO TODAY?
JAN 13

In a rambling, grievance-soaked address to the Detroit Economic Club, Donald Trump turned what was billed as an economic speech into a sprawling display of self-mythology, disinformation, and punitive demagoguery, offering not a governing vision but a warning about how power is being wielded.

What’s so corrosive about this speech is that it pretends to be an economic report while functioning as something else entirely: a loyalty ritual, a propaganda reel, and a scapegoating workshop—stitched together with numbers he tosses out like confetti and insults he deploys like punctuation. The setting is a business forum; Trump uses it as a throne room. He flatters the room as “the economic engine of America,” then immediately re-centers the story on himself: factories didn’t reopen because of investment cycles, labor markets, supply chains, or industrial policy—they reopened because he returned, because he “told you” it would happen, because he’s the protagonist of every balance sheet. Even his “jokes” (“You are so lucky I allow you into this room”) aren’t jokes; they’re test balloons for obedience. He does the authoritarian thing where he insults you, then laughs so you’ll laugh too, so complicity becomes part of the entertainment.

The most revealing thread is how he cannot speak about winning without also poisoning the concept of elections. He claims a “landslide,” claims the popular vote “all three times,” claims they “didn’t give us credit the second time,” then pivots to the lie that voter ID opposition equals a desire “to cheat”—as if democratic participation is suspicious unless it’s policed into submission. This is Trump’s so-called political genius and genuine moral rot in the same sentence: he recasts a policy debate into an accusation of criminal intent, and he does it in a room full of respectable people who are expected to nod along because the insult is aimed elsewhere. Then he extends the same rhetorical arson to his allies: he tells former Congressman Mike Rogers, “they rigged the election on you,” assures him “you won,” and performs faux reluctance (“I don’t like to be controversial”) while doing exactly what he always does—delegitimizing outcomes that don’t flatter him. It’s a con that never ends: even in victory, he still needs the grievance, because grievance is the product. The speech doesn’t just contain election disinformation; it normalizes it as casual small talk, a throwaway aside that cues the audience to treat democratic legitimacy as optional.

Economically, the address is a masterclass in manipulative vagueness: enormous claims, minimal verification, zero responsibility. He says the country went from “dead” to “hottest anywhere in the world,” that growth is “exploding,” productivity “soaring,” inflation “defeated,” incomes “rising,” and investment commitments hit “$18 trillion”—a number he repeats like a magic spell because it’s so large it dares you to question it. He throws out a “62%” trade deficit reduction, a “27%” budget deficit cut, “48 days in a row” of stock market highs, and a “5.4%” fourth-quarter GDP projection, then waves away any downside as “fake news” or “Democrat shutdown.” The purpose isn’t to explain; it’s to overwhelm. It’s the propaganda technique of saturating the space with big numbers so the audience feels informed without being able to evaluate a single claim. He doesn’t want scrutiny; he wants a fog machine.

His tantrum about the Federal Reserve is particularly ugly because it exposes what he thinks government is for: validating him. He frames rate decisions as sabotage—“they raise interest rates to try and kill it”—and then proposes a child’s version of monetary policy: good economic news should mean lower rates because it makes him feel good and makes the market go up. He calls the Fed chair a “jerk” and describes the institution as an obstacle to his desired aesthetic (stocks up, rates down, applause forever). This is the same impulse that shows up everywhere in the speech: any independent institution—elections, courts, the Fed, the press—exists in his mind either as a tool that serves him or a villain that must be smashed.

Then there’s the tariff fetish, which he sells with the confidence of someone who has never once been forced to reconcile rhetoric with reality. He insists tariffs aren’t paid by American consumers—foreign nations and “middlemen” supposedly pay—so the U.S. gets “hundreds of billions pouring into the Treasury” without pain. He wraps it in sepia nostalgia (“1887,” “McKinley,” “Teddy Roosevelt,” “we built the Panama Canal out of tariffs”), then adds the strongman flourish: even drug prices fall because he threatens other countries with tariffs until they “agree 100%.” It’s the same story every time: complex global systems reduced to a single lever controlled by a single man. The speech is basically “I threatened everyone and it worked,” over and over, in different costumes: trade policy, health policy, foreign policy, even supposedly “ending eight wars” through tariffs. Not only is it intellectually unserious—it’s dangerous, because it teaches supporters that coercion is governance and humiliation is diplomacy.

His Venezuela section is a perfect example of how Trump turns militarism into merchandising. He treats geopolitical violence like a highlight reel—“flawless” strikes, “wiped out” capacity, “as flawless an attack as there has ever been”—then mixes it with crude, transactional bragging about oil: they “said take it,” it’s “$5 billion,” “50 million barrels,” “the biggest ships,” “we’re bringing it in.” The whole thing reads like a mob boss recounting a heist, not a president describing actions that affect lives, sovereignty, and international stability. And he has the gall to declare that anyone who questions it “hates our country.” That’s not patriotism; it’s ideological blackmail: agree with me, or you’re an enemy.

The speech also repeatedly exposes his contempt for facts. He contradicts himself casually (“2,700 to 525,” then “2,700 to 550,” then “I think is the exact number”) because precision doesn’t matter when the point is domination. He calls out “the fake news” for corrections he’s inviting by refusing to be accurate, then uses the corrections as proof of persecution. It’s a closed loop: lie, get corrected, claim victimhood, demand applause. Even his asides about Biden being “high as a kite” aren’t just insults—they’re a signal that cruelty is the tone of governance. The crowd laughs, the press is demeaned, the political opponent is dehumanized, and the audience is trained to treat humiliation as leadership.

But the most vile portion—by far—is where he weaponizes “fraud” to paint immigrants, and specifically Somalis, as a collective criminal stain. He doesn’t talk about investigating specific networks, tightening oversight, improving audit systems, or ensuring due process. He talks about “the Somali population in Minnesota” as if an entire ethnicity is a syndicate. He claims “94% of them are in public assistance,” sneers that they “came from a place with nothing” and now drive Mercedes-Benzes, declares “they’re scammers” as an identity, and proposes blanket punitive measures: no wiring money out of the country, welfare cuts, citizenship revocation for fraud, “we’re not paying Minnesota,” and a DOJ “strike force” to “imprison any fraudster, politician, or public official.” This is classic demagogue strategy: take real concerns about fraud and wrap them around ethnic suspicion, so policy becomes a vehicle for prejudice. He even tosses in Somalia-as-pirates caricature—“all they have is murder and robbing ships”—to make the smear feel “natural.” It’s not just racist; it’s administratively violent. It primes the public to accept collective punishment, bureaucratic cruelty, and the erosion of rights as “common sense.”

He then drags named politicians into the mud—Ilhan Omar as a “total scam artist,” “AOC plus three,” “scammers”—not as critique, but as incitement. He isn’t disputing policy; he’s depicting opponents as criminals who deserve prison. That’s a hallmark of authoritarian speech: the opposition isn’t wrong; it’s illegitimate. The target isn’t debate; it’s elimination. And when he claims protesters are “fake riots,” “all practice,” rehearsed in hotel rooms, funded by shadowy forces “we pretty much know,” he’s laying down the familiar groundwork for repression: delegitimize dissent, then justify crackdowns as defense against a manufactured conspiracy. It’s McCarthyism updated with influencer cadence.

Even his culture-war detours are designed to degrade the audience’s moral reasoning. He uses trans athletes and women’s sports as a grotesque carnival story, exaggerating and sneering, because the point isn’t to protect women—it’s to keep the crowd angry and focused on a vulnerable out-group. He narrates imagined scenes of hulking men and tiny women, then says it’s “demeaning,” while he himself is doing the demeaning—turning people’s lives into a punchline to keep the audience primed for the next target. It’s emotional arson used to distract from the fact that he’s barely offering coherent economic policy.

Even when he touches on populist-sounding moves—credit card rate caps, mortgage bond purchases, premium subsidies—he frames them not as carefully designed interventions but as personal gifts. He talks about Obamacare as a “monstrosity,” claims insurers’ stock went up “more than 1,000%,” then insists he’ll route money “directly to the people” as if the only barrier to healthcare reform is the absence of his benevolent hand. He boasts drug prices will drop “300, 400, 500, 600%” (a mathematically ridiculous way to speak) and claims other countries instantly folded under tariff threats. Again: coercion as policy, hyperbole as proof, applause as accountability.

The speech also oozes contempt for governance norms. He talks about the Supreme Court potentially ruling on tariffs like it’s an affront to him personally—calling challengers “China-centric”—and implies he’ll “figure something out if we don’t win,” which is the authoritarian wink: law is a speed bump, not a boundary. He praises “merit” in hiring and college admissions in a way that reads like a culture-war dog whistle, not a serious workforce strategy. He mocks environmental standards as absurd, calls California leaders “communists,” and frames deregulation as a game where secretaries compete to cut rules—because in Trump’s world, fewer rules are always good, regardless of who gets harmed when oversight disappears.

Structurally, the address is a mess by design: it lurches from Detroit manufacturing to election conspiracies to Venezuela to the Fed to tariffs to women’s sports to Somali fraud to pirates to drug submarines to mortgage bonds to Obamacare to “balanced budget” fantasies. The incoherence is not accidental; it’s a strategy. If the speech were coherent, it could be evaluated. If it were grounded, it could be challenged. Instead, it’s a constant motion machine, a stream of claims and enemies and applause cues. He uses entertainment rhythms to short-circuit critical thinking. The crowd gets dopamine hits—insults, laughs, chants, villains—while the actual content remains vapor.

And the moral core of it—the part that should alarm anyone, regardless of party—is the way he consistently frames power as punishment and citizenship as conditional. He talks about revoking citizenship “fast,” cutting off payments to sanctuary cities, freezing welfare, imprisoning “politicians,” and treating whole communities as presumptive criminals. He doesn’t sound like a president describing policy; he sounds like a boss describing enforcement. He calls governors “crooked,” threatens states, and describes federal spending like a weapon—dispensed to loyal jurisdictions and withheld from disobedient ones. That is the language of a regime, not a republic.

So yes, it’s scathing because it deserves to be: this speech is not an economic vision. It’s a portrait of a leader who can’t stop lying, can’t stop demanding praise, can’t stop eroding trust in elections, can’t stop attacking independent institutions, and can’t stop feeding the crowd a rotating menu of scapegoats—immigrants, Democrats, the press, the Fed, courts—so he never has to answer for the chaos his own style creates. The Detroit Economic Club invited him to talk about the economy; he gave them a sermon about himself, a warning about his enemies, and a demonstration of how easily “policy” becomes a vehicle for cruelty when the point is domination rather than governance.
…and quite a thing for a beloved vulnerable parent to be betrayed by self serving adult children under the guise of (false) moral loyalty.

Facts About The Meatmen 

1. Origin
The Meatmen are an American punk rock band from Lansing, Michigan.
The band was formed in 1981.

2. Genre and Style
Their music is rooted in hardcore punk, with elements of punk rock, shock rock, and satire.
They are especially known for offensive, provocative, and sarcastic lyrics, often meant to mock social norms and censorship.

3. Frontman
The band was founded and led by Tesco Vee, who is the main vocalist and songwriter.
Tesco Vee is also known as the co-founder of Touch and Go Records, an influential independent punk label.

4. Lyrical Themes
The Meatmen’s lyrics frequently include:
Dark humor
Political satire
Social criticism
Deliberately shocking content
Many songs are intentionally exaggerated to challenge political correctness and moral authority.

5. Notable Releases
Some well-known albums include:
“Blood Sausage” (1982)
“War of the Super Bikes” (1985)
“Rock ’n’ Roll Juggernaut” (1986)
“Pope on a Rope” (1990)

6. Reputation
The Meatmen are considered one of the most controversial bands in punk history.
They were frequently criticized and banned by venues due to lyrical content but also praised for their fearless DIY attitude.

7. Influence
The band influenced many hardcore punk and alternative rock musicians, especially in the U.S. underground scene.
Their work reflects the raw, rebellious spirit of early 1980s American hardcore punk.

8. Current Status
The Meatmen have reformed multiple times and continue to perform live occasionally, mainly led by Tesco Vee.
Short Summary
The Meatmen are a hardcore punk band from the United States, formed in 1981, known for offensive humor, political satire, and a confrontational punk attitude.

10 Bahaya Bid’ah dalam Agama

Bid’ah dalam agama adalah perkara yang dilarang oleh Allah dan Rasul-Nya. Bid’ah di sini adalah tata cara beragama yang tidak ada tuntunannya dari syari’at. Imam Asy-Syathibi (wafat 790 H) menjelaskan definisi bid’ah sebagai berikut:

طريقة في الدين مخترعة تضاهي الشرعية، يقصَد بالسلوك عليها المبالغة في التعبد لله سبحانه

“Bid’ah adalah sebuah tata cara beragama yang diada-adakan, menyerupai syariat, dilakukan dengan maksud berlebih-lebihan dalam ibadah kepada Allah Subhanah.” (Al-I’tisham, 1/37)

Bid’ah dalam agama selain terlarang juga memberikan bahaya bagi pelakunya. Di antaranya berikut ini:

Pertama: Amalan bid’ah-nya tertolak
Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

مَنْ أَحْدَثَ فِى أَمْرِنَا هَذَا مَا لَيْسَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ رَدٌّ

“Barangsiapa membuat suatu perkara baru dalam urusan kami ini (urusan agama) yang tidak ada asalnya, maka perkara tersebut tertolak.” (HR. Bukhari no. 2697 dan Muslim no. 1718)

Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلاً لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ

“Barangsiapa melakukan suatu amalan yang bukan berasal dari kami, maka amalan tersebut tertolak.” (HR. Muslim no. 1718)

Kedua: Bid’ah merupakan kesesatan
Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam setiap memulai khotbah biasanya beliau mengucapkan,

أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الْحَدِيثِ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ وَخَيْرُ الْهُدَى هُدَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَشَرُّ الأُمُورِ مُحْدَثَاتُهَا وَكُلُّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلاَلَةٌ

“Amma ba’du. Sesungguhnya sebaik-baik perkataan adalah Kitabullah dan sebaik-baik petunjuk adalah petunjuk Muhammad shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam. Sejelek-jelek perkara adalah (perkara agama) yang diada-adakan, setiap (perkara agama) yang diada-adakan itu adalah bid’ah, setiap bid’ah adalah kesesatan.” (HR. Muslim no. 867)

Dalam riwayat An-Nasa’i,

مَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَلا مُضِلَّ لَهُ ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلا هَادِيَ لَهُ ، إِنَّ أَصَدَقَ الْحَدِيثِ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ ، وَأَحْسَنَ الْهَدْيِ هَدْيُ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، وَشَرَّ الأُمُورِ مُحْدَثَاتُهَا ، وَكُلَّ مُحْدَثَةٍ بِدْعَةٌ ، وَكُلَّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلالَةٌ ، وَكُلَّ ضَلالَةٍ فِي النَّارِ

“Barangsiapa yang diberi petunjuk oleh Allah maka tidak ada yang bisa menyesatkannya. Dan yang disesatkan oleh Allah tidak ada yang bisa memberi petunjuk padanya. Sesungguhnya sebenar-benar perkataan adalah Kitabullah dan sebaik-baik petunjuk adalah petunjuk Muhammad shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam. Sejelek-jelek perkara adalah (perkara agama) yang diada-adakan, setiap (perkara agama) yang diada-adakan itu adalah bid’ah, setiap bid’ah adalah kesesatan, dan setiap kesesatan tempatnya di neraka.” (HR. An-Nasa’i no. 1578, disahihkan oleh Al-Albani dalam Shahih wa Dha’if Sunan An-Nasa’i)

Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

أُوصِيكُمْ بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ وَالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ وَإِنْ عَبْدًا حَبَشِيًّا فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ يَعِشْ مِنْكُمْ بَعْدِى فَسَيَرَى اخْتِلاَفًا كَثِيرًا فَعَلَيْكُمْ بِسُنَّتِى وَسُنَّةِ الْخُلَفَاءِ الْمَهْدِيِّينَ الرَّاشِدِينَ تَمَسَّكُوا بِهَا وَعَضُّوا عَلَيْهَا بِالنَّوَاجِذِ وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَمُحْدَثَاتِ الأُمُورِ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ مُحْدَثَةٍ بِدْعَةٌ وَكُلَّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلاَلَةٌ

“Aku wasiatkan kepada kalian untuk bertakwa kepada Allah, tetap mendengar dan taat kepada pemimpin walaupun yang memimpin kalian adalah seorang budak dari Habasyah. Karena barangsiapa di antara kalian yang hidup sepeninggalku nanti, dia akan melihat perselisihan yang banyak. Maka, wajib bagi kalian untuk berpegang pada sunahku dan sunah Khulafa’ur Rasyidin yang mereka itu telah diberi petunjuk. Berpegang teguhlah dengannya dan gigitlah ia dengan gigi geraham kalian. Jauhilah dengan perkara (agama) yang diada-adakan karena setiap perkara (agama) yang diada-adakan adalah bid’ah dan setiap bid’ah adalah kesesatan.” (HR. At-Tirmidzi no. 2676. ia berkata, “Hadis ini hasan sahih”)

Ketiga: Pelaku bid’ah sulit bertobat
Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

إِنَ اللهَ حَجَبَ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ كُلِّ صَاحِبِ بِدْعَةٍ حَتَّى يَدَعْ بِدْعَتَهُ

“Sungguh Allah menghalangi tobat dari setiap pelaku bid’ah sampai ia meninggalkan bid’ahnya.”  (HR. Ath-Thabrani dalam Al-Ausath no.4334. Disahihkan oleh Al-Albani dalam Shahih At-Targhib wa At-Tarhib no. 54)

Keempat: Terhalangi dari telaga Rasulullah
Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

أَنَا فَرَطُكُمْ عَلَى الْحَوْضِ ، لَيُرْفَعَنَّ إِلَىَّ رِجَالٌ مِنْكُمْ حَتَّى إِذَا أَهْوَيْتُ لأُنَاوِلَهُمُ اخْتُلِجُوا دُونِى فَأَقُولُ أَىْ رَبِّ أَصْحَابِى . يَقُولُ لاَ تَدْرِى مَا أَحْدَثُوا بَعْدَكَ

“Aku akan mendahului kalian di Al-Haudh (telaga). Lalu ditampakkan di hadapanku beberapa orang di antara kalian. Ketika aku akan mengambilkan (minuman) untuk mereka dari Al-Haudh, mereka dijauhkan dariku. Aku lantas berkata, ‘Wahai Rabbku, ini adalah umatku’. Allah berfirman, ‘Engkau tidak tahu (bid’ah) yang mereka ada-adakan sepeninggalmu.’“ (HR. Bukhari no. 6576, 7049)

Dalam riwayat lain disebutkan,

إِنَّهُمْ مِنِّى . فَيُقَالُ إِنَّكَ لاَ تَدْرِى مَا بَدَّلُوا بَعْدَكَ فَأَقُولُ سُحْقًا سُحْقًا لِمَنْ بَدَّلَ بَعْدِى

“(Wahai Rabb), sungguh mereka bagian dari pengikutku.” Lalu, Allah berfirman, “Sungguh engkau tidak tahu bahwa sepeninggalmu mereka telah mengganti ajaranmu.” Kemudian Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam mengatakan, “Celaka, celaka bagi orang yang telah mengganti ajaranku sesudahku.” (HR. Bukhari no. 7050)

Al-’Aini ketika menjelaskan hadis ini, beliau berkata, “Hadis-hadis yang menjelaskan orang-orang yang demikian, yaitu yang dikenal oleh Nabi sebagai umatnya, namun ada penghalang antara mereka dan Nabi, dikarenakan yang mereka ada-adakan setelah Nabi wafat. Ini menunjukkan setiap orang mengada-adakan suatu perkara dalam agama yang tidak diridai Allah itu tidak termasuk jemaah kaum muslimin.

Seluruh ahlul bid’ah itu adalah orang-orang yang gemar mengganti (ajaran agama) dan mengada-ada, juga orang-orang zalim dan ahli maksiat, mereka bertentangan dengan Al-Haq.

Orang-orang yang melakukan itu semua, yaitu mengganti (ajaran agama) dan mengada-ada apa yang tidak ada ajarannya dalam Islam termasuk dalam bahasan hadis ini.” (Umdatul Qari, 6/10)

Kelima: Bid’ah merupakan maksiat
Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

انَّهُ سَيَلِي أَمْرَكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِي رِجَالٌ يُطْفِئُونَ السُّنَّةَ ، وَيُحْدِثُونَ بِدْعَةً ، وَيُؤَخِّرُونَ الصَّلَاةَ عَنْ مَوَاقِيتِهَا ” ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ : يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، كَيْفَ بِي إِذَا أَدْرَكْتُهُمْ ؟ قَالَ : ” لَيْسَ يَا ابْنَ أُمِّ عَبْدٍ طَاعَةٌ لِمَنْ عَصَى اللَّهَ ” ، قَالَهَا ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ

“Sungguh di antara perkara yang akan datang pada kalian sepeninggalku nanti, yaitu akan ada orang (pemimpin) yang mematikan sunah dan membuat bid’ah. Mereka juga mengakhirkan salat dari waktu sebenarnya.” Ibnu Mas’ud lalu bertanya, “Apa yang mesti kami perbuat jika kami menemui mereka?” Nabi bersabda, “Wahai anak Adam, tidak ada ketaatan pada orang yang bermaksiat pada Allah.” Beliau mengatakannya 3 kali. (HR. Ahmad no.3659, Ibnu Majah no.2860. Disahihkan Al-Albani dalam Silsilah Ahadits Shahihah, 2864).

Keenam: Mendapatkan dosa jariyah
Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

إِنَّهُ مَنْ أَحْيَا سُنَّةً مِنْ سُنَّتِي قَدْ أُمِيتَتْ بَعْدِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَجْرِ مِثْلَ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَنْقُصَ مِنْ أُجُورِهِمْ شَيْئًا ، وَمَنِ ابْتَدَعَ بِدْعَةَ ضَلَالَةٍ لَا يَرْضَاهَا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِثْلُ آثَامِ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا لَا يَنْقُصُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَوْزَارِ النَّاسِ شَيْئًا

“Barangsiapa yang sepeninggalku menghidupkan sebuah sunah yang aku ajarkan, maka ia akan mendapatkan pahala semisal dengan pahala orang-orang yang melakukannya tanpa mengurangi pahala mereka sedikit pun. Barangsiapa yang membuat sebuah bid’ah dhalalah yang tidak diridai oleh Allah dan Rasul-Nya, maka ia akan mendapatkan dosa semisal dengan dosa orang-orang yang melakukannya tanpa mengurangi dosa mereka sedikit pun.” (HR. Tirmidzi no.2677, ia berkata: “Hadis ini hasan.”)

Ketujuh: Merebaknya bid’ah merupakan tanda akhir zaman
Hadis dari Hudzaifah Ibnul Yaman radhiyallahu ‘anhu, ia berkata,

يا رسولَ اللهِ ! إنا كنا بشرٌ . فجاء اللهُ بخيرٍ . فنحن فيه . فهل من وراءِ هذا الخيرِ شرٌّ ؟ قال ( نعم ) قلتُ : هل من وراءِ ذلك الشرِّ خيرٌ ؟ قال ( نعم ) قلتُ : فهل من وراءِ ذلك الخيرِ شرٌّ ؟ قال ( نعم ) قلتُ : كيف ؟ قال ( يكون بعدي أئمةٌ لا يهتدون بهدايَ ، ولا يستنُّون بسُنَّتي . وسيقوم فيهم رجالٌ قلوبُهم قلوبُ الشياطينِ في جُثمانِ إنسٍ ) قال قلتُ : كيف أصنعُ ؟ يا رسولَ اللهِ ! إن أدركت ُذلك ؟ قال ( تسمعُ وتطيع للأميرِ . وإن ضَرَب ظهرَك . وأخذ مالَك . فاسمعْ وأطعْ )

“Wahai Rasulullah, dulu kami orang biasa. Lalu, Allah mendatangkan kami kebaikan (berupa Islam), dan kami sekarang berada dalam keislaman. Apakah setelah semua ini akan datang kejelekan?”

Nabi bersabda, “Ya.”

“Apakah setelah itu akan datang kebaikan?”

Nabi bersabda, “Ya.”

“Apakah setelah itu akan datang kejelekan?”

Nabi bersabda, “Ya.”

Aku bertanya, “Apa itu?”

Nabi bersabda, “Akan datang para pemimpin yang tidak berpegang pada petunjukku dan tidak berpegang pada sunnahku. Akan hidup di antara mereka orang-orang yang hatinya adalah hati setan namun berjasad manusia.”

Aku bertanya, “Apa yang mesti kami perbuat wahai Rasulullah jika mendapati mereka?”

Nabi bersabda, “Tetaplah mendengar dan taat kepada penguasa, walau mereka memukul punggungmu atau mengambil hartamu, tetaplah mendengar dan taat.” (HR. Muslim no.1847)

Tidak berpegang pada sunah Nabi dalam beragama artinya ia berpegang pada sunah-sunah yang berasal dari selain Allah dan Rasul-Nya, yang merupakan ke-bid’ah-an.

Kedelapan: Disebut sebagai bukan golongan Nabi
Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam bersabda,

جَاءَ ثَلَاثَةُ رَهْطٍ إِلَى بُيُوتِ أَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَسْأَلُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَةِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَلَمَّا أُخْبِرُوا كَأَنَّهُمْ تَقَالُّوهَا ، فَقَالُوا : وَأَيْنَ نَحْنُ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَدْ غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ ؟ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمْ : أَمَّا أَنَا ، فَإِنِّي أُصَلِّي اللَّيْلَ أَبَدًا ، وَقَالَ آخَرُ : أَنَا أَصُومُ الدَّهْرَ وَلَا أُفْطِرُ ، وَقَالَ آخَرُ : أَنَا أَعْتَزِلُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَا أَتَزَوَّجُ أَبَدًا ، فَجَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِلَيْهِمْ ، فَقَالَ : ” أَنْتُمُ الَّذِينَ قُلْتُمْ كَذَا وَكَذَا ، أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَخْشَاكُمْ لِلَّهِ وَأَتْقَاكُمْ لَهُ لَكِنِّي أَصُومُ وَأُفْطِرُ ، وَأُصَلِّي وَأَرْقُدُ ، وَأَتَزَوَّجُ النِّسَاءَ ، فَمَنْ رَغِبَ عَنْ سُنَّتِي فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي

Ada tiga orang mendatangi rumah istri-istri Nabi shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam dan bertanya tentang ibadah Nabi shallallahu ’alaihi wasallam. Setelah diberitakan kepada mereka, sepertinya mereka merasa hal itu masih sedikit bagi mereka.

Mereka berkata, “Ibadah kita tak ada apa-apanya dibanding Rasulullah shallallahu ’alaihi wasallam. Bukankah beliau sudah diampuni dosa-dosanya yang telah lalu dan juga yang akan datang?”

Salah seorang dari mereka berkata, “Sungguh, aku akan salat malam selama-lamanya (tanpa tidur).”

Kemudian yang lain berkata, “Kalau aku, sungguh aku akan berpuasa Dahr (setahun penuh) dan aku tidak akan berbuka.”

Dan yang lain lagi berkata, “Aku akan menjauhi wanita dan tidak akan menikah selama-lamanya”.

Kemudian datanglah Rasulullah shallallahu ’alaihi wasallam kepada mereka seraya bertanya, “Kalian berkata begini dan begitu. Adapun aku, demi Allah, adalah orang yang paling takut kepada Allah di antara kalian, dan juga paling bertakwa. Aku berpuasa dan juga berbuka, aku salat dan juga tidur serta menikahi wanita. Barangsiapa yang benci sunahku, maka bukanlah dari golonganku.” (HR. Bukhari no.5063)

Kesembilan: Bid’ah itu merusak hati
Syaikhul Islam Ibnu Taimiyah rahimahullah mengatakan,

الشرائع أغذية القلوب، فمتى اغتذت القلوب بالبدع، لم يبق فيها فضل للسنن، فتكون بمنزلة من اغتذى بالطعام الخبيث

“Syariat-syariat Islam (yang sahih) adalah gizi yang menyehatkan hati. Ketika anda memberi nutrisi bagi hati anda berupa kebid’ahan, maka tidak akan ada lagi keutamaan sunah-sunah Nabi dalam hati anda. Ini sebagaimana orang yang makan makanan yang buruk.” (Iqtidha Shiratil Mustaqim, 2/104)

Kesepuluh: Mematikan sunah dan menjauhkan darinya
Seorang tabi’in, Hasan bin ‘Athiyah rahimahullah mengatakan,

ما ابتدع قوم بدعة في دينهم إلا نزع الله من سنتهم مثلها ولا يعيدها إليهم إلى يوم القيامة

“Tidaklah suatu kaum melakukan suatu perkara yang diada-adakan dalam urusan agama mereka (bid’ah) melainkan Allah akan mencabut suatu sunah yang semisal dari lingkungan mereka. Allah tidak akan mengembalikan sunah itu kepada mereka sampai kiamat.” (Lammud Durril Mantsur, hal. 21).

Ibnul Jauzi (wafat tahun 597H) berkata,

وقد لبس إبليس عَلَى خلق كثير من العوام يحضرون مجالس الذكر ويبكون ويكتفون بذلك ظنا منهم أن المقصود إنما هو العمل وإذا لم يعمل بما يسمع كان زيادة فِي الحجة عَلَيْهِ وأني لأعرف خلقا يحضرون المجلس منذ سنين ويبكون ويخشعون ولا يتغير أحدهم عما قد اعتاده من المعاملة فِي الربا والغش فِي البيع والجهل بأركان الصلاة والغيبة للمسلمين والعقوق للوالدين

“Iblis telah menipu kebanyakan orang awam, yaitu mereka yang menghadiri majelis-majelis yang membuat mereka menangis dan mereka merasa puas dengannya. Mereka menyangka itulah tujuan dan itulah amalan kebaikan. Jika mereka tidak mengamalkan apa yang mereka dengan dalam majelis-majelis itu, mereka akan dituntut di akhirat kelak. Dan sungguh aku mengenal orang yang menghadiri majelis-majelis tersebut bertahun-tahun, menangis dan merasa puas dengannya, namun tidak ada yang berubah dari kebiasaannya bermuamalah riba, berbuat curang dalam jual-beli, jahil terhadap rukun-rukun salat, menggibahi orang lain, dan durhaka terhadap orang tua.” (Talbis Iblis, 1/348)

Demikian sebagian bahaya bid’ah yang mengancam pelakunya. Semoga membuat kita semakin takut dan waspada terhadap ke-bid’ah-an dan semakin semangat menjalankan apa-apa yang dituntunkan oleh Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wasallam.

Wallahu waliyyut taufiq was-sadad.

Stop Defending Jesus: Walk Him Into Our World
Copyright ©️ Naked Reflections with Tarryn Bell 

Stop running to defend your Faith shall I say our precious Lord and Christ. 
Jesus does not need defending, and society no longer needs fire-and-fury Christianity.
That approach has done profound harm. Fear-mongering and guilt have shaped generations of believers who struggle to see God as loving. I know this intimately.

I too had had a life-long with forgiveness because the God I was introduced to stood with a whip in His hand, ready to send me to hell if I failed. He was mostly grumpy and mean. Beloved, that was not liberation that was control and manipulation. And...I am still unlearning sadly. 

The Christian call is not to defend Jesus, but to imitate Him. It really is that simple!
Yet somewhere along the line particularly through colonisation we were introduced to a Westernised version of God that must be enforced and shoved down the throats of anyone!  Certainly it was for control but the spirituality that existed here was part of life. Why was the white God so suspicious of, even hostile toward, Eastern and African traditions. A God framed through empire rather than incarnation.

Consider this honestly,  what if Jesus had been incarnated in the heart of Africa? How strange—perhaps even foolish would it be for white Europeans today, in a post-modern world, to rigidly follow African Tradition Religion? It defintely wouldn't be sinful but it would be deeply disconnected from context. And yet, this is precisely what has been demanded of many African believers, to abandon their cultural worldviews in favour of a foreign expression of faith, presented as universal and absolute. Of course not all ideologies brings honour to God but certainly even traits in American🇺🇲 and
European🇦🇨 Christianity! 

This is why we must return to the theological basics:
1. #ContextMatters.
Scripture was written for us but it was not written to us. We were never the first recipients of the Holy Bible. The Bible emerged within specific historical, political, and cultural realities. Ignoring that does not honour the text; it distorts it. Wholly so!

2. #Application is a #Skill.
Faithful reading requires discernment. We must ask, with the help of the Holy Spirit: "What does this mean today"? What do kingship, war narratives, parables, rites of passage, or even prayer shawls mean in our context now?
Hermeneutics matters and theology requires both devotion and discipline.

Furthermore, we must ask a harder question still:
What does this Period of our lives require, the year 2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣?
We are living in a time of fractured families, lost hope, substance abuse, social media saturation, influencers, supposed influencers and bad influence. A deep moral and economic fatigue. Or people are poor in many facets of their lives. 

 In SA🇿🇦, trauma is not abstract it is inherited, systemic, and personal. How would Jesus walk today in Cape Town? On the Cape Flats? Along the Sea Point promenade? In Limpopo, where children still drown in pit latrines?
What would Jesus say to church leadership that keeps people busy from Monday to Sunday with “spiritual formation,” while the City around them continues to crumble in decay?
People are not longing for more rules, nor for endless lists of what not to do. They are yearning for real connection. For an invitation to be loved, forgiven, restored. They are desperate for spaces where trauma can be named and healed. Where wounds that run through almost every family generation in this country are treated with compassion rather than condemnation.

The question before us is not, “How loudly can we proclaim Jesus?”
It is, “How faithfully can we walk like Him?”
So, what does it mean today to show up for my brother or my sister even the one who has wronged me, does not look like me, or does not share my customs or ideologies? Even those who do not smell like me. 

What does love look like when it costs me comfort, certainty, or moral superiority and inheritant privilege?
The era of loudhailing Jesus on buses and trains is losing relevance, not because Jesus has lost power but because His name has been so often misrepresented from pulpits. Words have become cheap where lives contradict them.

I believe the time we are in now calls for something far more radical:

🙏🏽To walk like Jesus—often without words.
🙏🏽To be present.
🙏🏽To be just.
🙏🏽To be merciful.
🙏🏽To rebuild what has been broken

Because the world will not be convinced by how well we defend Christ, or how loud we scream his name but by how closely our lives resemble His.
A true encounter with him that leaves people shouting I HAVE MET A MAN AND HE HAS TRULY CHANGED MY LIFE. 

LET US Stop Defending Jesus BELOVED, BUT COURAGEOUSLY Walk Him Into Our World!🌎

Buku The Prophet (Sang Nabi) adalah karya Khalil Gibran dalam Bahasa Inggris yang paling terkenal yang pertama kali diterbitkan di New York tahun 1923. 

Dari judul buku karya klasik abad 20 itu, para pembacanya menjulukki Khalil Gibran sebagai The Immortal Prophet of Libanon (Sang Nabi Abadi dari Libanon).

Yah, Kahlil Gibran aslinya memang orang Libanon dan beliau juga menulis dalam Bahasa Arab, karyanya yang terkenal diantaranya adalah Al-Ajnihah Al-Mutakasirah (Sayap-Sayap Patah) dan Al-Arwahul-Mutamarridah (Jiwa-Jiwa memberontak).

Buku berjudul  “Jiwa-Jiwa Memberontak” ini berisi kumpulan cerita-cerita pendek. Dan salah satu yang paling menarik saya adalah yang diberi judul “Khalil Al-Kafir/Khalil si Bocah Kufur”. Beliau memakai namanya sendiri sebagai tokoh ceritanya.

Lewat tokoh bernama Khalil ini, pemberontakan terhadap budaya feodal yang bersekutu dengan para pendeta dimulai. Khalil ditendang keluar dari biara/gereja, karena dia tahu isi kebusukan di dalamnya. 

Bagimana aturan penguasa yang di legitimasi gereja berubah jadi cakar-cakar yang membelenggu kebebasan hidup dan suara hati nurani. Jadi alat menindas, menjajah, membodohi dan merampas harta rakyat. Dan  siapapun yang berani melawan/memberontak, akan di cap  melawan Tuhan???.

Jadi si Khalil  ini menelanjangi aneka kebusukan yang ada dibalik biara yang suka dianggap sebagai tempat berkumpulnya orang-orang suci. Jadi sepertinya lucu juga, jika ada orang Islam tidak mau membaca karya Khalil Gibran hanya karena beliau bukan Seorang Muslim.

Atau mungkin sebagai sesama agama Samawi, orang-orang Islam ketika membaca karya-karya Khalil Gibran : Juga hanya merasa ditelanjangi, diperlihatkan kebusukan-kebusukan dirinya sendiri yang suka dibalut dengan Kesucian Agama???.

Nih, saya kutipkan sedikit pemberontakan  dalam “Si Khalil Bocah Kufur” ;  Mereka membuat tanda salib dengan tangan kanan sambil meremas kalbumu dengan tangan kirinya. Inilah uskup yang kalian angkat menjadi pembantu tapi berubah menjadi tuan. Diangkat menjadi wali tapi berubah menjadi beban yang berat. Seperti inikah pemimpin bagi orang-orang Nasrani?. Para pendeta yang suka menghisap darah orang-orang miskin.

Mereka adalah para penjual ayat dan barang siapa yang tidak mau membelinya, akan di cap kufur kepada Allah dan nabi-nabinya dan tidak bisa mencicipi nikmatnya surga?.

Yah, mereka berkotbah tentang kesucian langit, tapi pikiran mereka sebenarnya merayap ke sakumu bagaikan seekor ular!!! 

Ini Khalil menceritakan keadaan didalam biara orang Kristiani loh, bukan keadaan di dalam Ruang Ibadah atau Pondok Pesantren Orang Islam.

#info #fyi Kedutaan Besar AS di Tehran disandera Demonstran, Bagaimana Nasib Kedutaan Besar Uni Soviet di Tehran ?

Ketika Kedutaan Besar AS di Tehran diserang oleh Massa Demonstran pro Revolusi, Pasukan pro Revolusi menyandera 63 diplomat dan 3 WN AS di dalam Kedutaan Besar AS pada November 1979. Pemerintah AS menjalankan sebuah Operasi Penyelamatan Sandera yang bernama Operation Eagle Claw yang berakhir gagal karena Helikopter Pasukan AS ada yang jatuh karena kena badai gurun  

Lalu yang jadi pertanyaan adalah bagaimana nasib Kedutaan Besar Uni Soviet ? 

Banyak yang tidak tahu bahwa sebenarnya Ayatollah Khomeini itu juga tidak simpatik bahkan anti dengan Uni Soviet pada masa itu karena menyerang Afghanistan pada Desember 1979, Lalu Ayatollah Khomeini sendiri juga menyatakan bahwa Uni Soviet bukanlah role model ideal. Apalagi mengingat Mujahidin El Khalq (MEK) yang dipimpin oleh Massoud Rajavi dan Maryam Rajavi ini merupakan Organisasi Kiri yang dulu ikut Revolusi Iran tapi akhirnya menentang Ayatollah Khomeini karena tidak sejakan pemikiran nya, MEK akhirnya berkoalisi dengan Saddam Hussein di Irak dan dipersenjatai Saddam dalam Perang Irak Iran 

Kembali ke topik utama, Apa yang terjadi pada Kedutaan Uni Soviet di Tehran ? 

Berdasarkan arsip sejarah dan kesaksian intelijen, Sebenarnya Kedutaan Besar Uni Soviet di Tehran pada waktu itu juga mau diserang para Demonstran. Akan tetapi,  Duta Besar Soviet di Teheran (Vladimir Vinogradov) atau Kepala Stasiun KGB setempat menyampaikan pesan langsung kepada orang-orang kepercayaan Khomeini yaitu 

"Jika satu saja diplomat kami kehilangan sehelai rambut, atau jika kedutaan kami disentuh, kami tidak akan memberlakukan sanksi ekonomi. Kami akan menargetkan kalian secara pribadi."

Soviet mengancam bahwa rudal-rudal Scud atau tim pembunuh KGB sudah mengunci koordinat rumah para Ayatollah dan Mullah senior di Qom dan Teheran apabila satu jari pun masuk ke Kedutaan Besar Soviet di Tehran. 

Metode ini terbukti validitasnya dari insiden serupa di Beirut tahun 1985. Ketika diplomat Soviet diculik Hezbullah, KGB tidak bernegosiasi. Mereka menculik kerabat pemimpin penculik itu, memotong salah satu bagian tubuhnya, dan mengirimkannya ke pemimpin tersebut dengan pesan " lepaskan orang kami atau sisanya akan menyusul ". 🎤 Janis Joplin, raw and fearless under the lights.

But the real power of Woodstock wasn’t in the performances — it was in the people. A crowd that proved love could be louder than war, and harmony stronger than hate.

This video brings it all back — the chaos, the calm, the connection.
Because Woodstock wasn’t just music. It was a message that still matters.

Hiç kimsenin dini inançlarından dolayı (kafir, müşrik, münafık, agnostik, ateist, deist her ne ise) bu dünyada insanlar tarafından cezalandırılamayacağına inanıyorum. Bu saha hukukullah sahasıdır. Allah'ın hakkına girer. Cezayı da O verir. Cezası da Ahirete tehir edilmiştir.

İnsanlar insanları ancak ve ancak, bireylere ve topluma karşı işledikleri suçlardan dolayı cezalandırabilir. Cezalandırılmalıdır da. Yani "hukuk'ul-ibad /kul hakları" söz konusu olduğunda taviz verilemez! 

"Müşrikleri nerede bulursanız öldürün, yakalayıp hapsedin, onları gözetim altında tutun,.” [Tevbe/5] Ayette öldürülmesi gereken kimseler Müşriklerin eşkiyalarıdır. Buradaki emir; "müşriklerin öldürülmesini" değil, bu mütecaviz, saldırgan kimselerin öldürülmesidir. Hatta ayet bir ültimatomdur! Gözdağıdır. Bildiğiniz, yıldırma politikasıdır. Psikolojik taktiktir!  Hiç kimse Müslüman olması için zorlanamaz! “Artık dileyen iman etsin, dileyen inkâr etsin…” [Kehf/29] İman kalben tasdiktir. Yani gönüllülük esastır. Dinde zorlama yoktur!

“Yeryüzünde fitne kalmayıncaya kadar Müşriklerle savaşın.” [Bakara/193] gibi ayetlerdeki FİTNE; esas itibariyle din ve vicdan hürriyetini kaldırmaktır. İşte din ve vicdan hürriyetini kaldıran zorbalara karşı mücadele edin demektir! [Buruc/ 10, Nahl/ 110] ayetlerinde fitne kelimesi; "müminlere işkence yapmak" anlamında kullanılmıştır!

“Fitne, öldürmekten daha beterdir.” [Bakara/191] Öldürmekten daha büyük olan fitne; Taberi'ye göre, şirktir. Ki bu fitne (şirk); müminleri dinlerinden döndürmeyi amaçlayan, onların şirk koşmalarını sağlamayı hedefleyen bir musibet, baskı ve terör anlamındaki fitnedir.
Yani; Müminin dininden dönüp müşrik olması, öldürülmesinden daha beterdir.

[Tevbe/5] teki ayet; antlaşmayı bozan, Müslümanlara savaş açmış mütecaviz, muharip kimseleri kapsamına almaktadır. Yoksa bu ayet; fitneyi şirk ile denk sayıp, şirkten daha beter görmek ve böylece bütün müşrikler Müslüman oluncaya kadar onlarla savaşmak, onları öldürmek şeklinde bir emir değildir! Peygamberimizin sünneti /uygulaması da bu şekildedir!

Nitekim eğer ayet yeryüzünde fitne /şirk kalmayıncaya kadar Müşrikleri katledin olsaydı, Peygamberimiz Arabistan yarımadasında yüz binlerce insanı öldürmesi icap ederdi. Oysa o üç milyon toprağı fethetmesine rağmen sadece, 250 kadar saldırganı öldürmüştür. Müslümanlar da bu kadar büyük bir toprak parçasını fethetmelerine rağmen toplam 150 kadar şehit /kayıp verdiler. Ki bu rakamlar bize, o günün savaşları göz önüne alındığında çok az zayiat ile, bu fetihlerin gerçekleştirildiğini göstermektedir. Demek amaç müşrikleri öldürmek olmayıp, onları İslam'ın sulh ve sukununa davet etmektir.

Demek FİTNE; Müşriklerin Müslümanları şirke döndürmek için uyguladıkları BASKI'dır! Demek "Öldürmekten beter olan fitne" Müminin dininden dönüp müşrik olmasıdır. Bu ise, öldürülmesinden daha beterdir.

In the aftermath of the Bondi terrorist attack the Albanese Labor government is introducing hate speech laws next week in Parliament in a Bill and explanation that is nearly 500 pages long.
 
These laws have been rushed with inadequate consultation with organisations, politicians, national security agencies and the general public.
 
Over the past four years we’ve seen how – time and time again – this government has rushed bills through only to see them fail to address the real problem. For example: the bill to address the release of detainees from detention centres just a few years ago.  Many had heinous criminal offences and some reoffended after release yet nothing was done, and the rushed bill was a failure. 
 
This is no doubt another one of those bills, but worse. Australians will be stripped of their freedom of speech, opinion and ability to express the pride they have in their culture and nationality.
 
I want to explain to the people my grave concerns about this manipulative, controlling, politically driven piece of legislation. It needs to be called out, and people have a right to be informed.
 
The PM wants to appear that he has Australians concerns at heart but when the public have less than two days to make a submission to a snap inquiry on the legislation, it’s obvious he is not interested in what you have to say.
 
Do I always get it right? No, but I am trying to inform you. Look at what's happened to a councillors in Britain for saying she was 'born and bred' there. It is up to you to fight back and send in a submission opposing this legislation, or accept it and live with the consequences. 

Here are some concerns I have with just one section, 80.2BF.

‘Intimidation’, which is not defined in the Bill, and ‘to fear harassment’ are two very low bars that mean almost anything could be made a criminal offence. 'Fear' is a personal expression and we have seen in domestic violence courts that no evidence is needed to prove someone is in fear, so where is the onus of proof here. ‘Hatred’ is also very open to interpretation and vague.

So to criticise the immigration program and say migrants from certain countries shouldn't be accepted into Australia will be an offence. Government has recently put tougher requirements on student visas from India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan - haven't they just committed an offence based on someone's national origin?

Talking about banning the burqa certainly will be an offence.

Criticising the immigration program would probably be an offence because that may cause migrants to feel intimidated because of their national origin.

Subsection (1)(b)(ii) could make someone saying ‘Australia is the best country in the world’ a criminal subject to 5 years in prison. Will flying the Australian flag be an offence as well? That’s disseminating ideas of superiority (the best) over a group of people based on their national origin (not being Australian).

Subsection (3) says for the purposes of subsection 1 it is IMMATERIAL for the offence whether anyone actually felt intimidated or feared harassment, or even whether they were the national or ethnic origin targeted.

Subsection (4) means - quoting from the religious texts of Islam that call for violence on other people would be exempted from the offence. So some of the worst calls to violence would still go unpunished. 

These powers are huge and could be weaponised against everyday Australians. Do you trust politicians with this power? I don’t.

Perjalanan Salib Paroki St. Peter, Kudat

📍 Simpang Mengayau, Kudat
📅 10 Januari 2025
✝️ Selebran: Rev. Fr. Rayner

Perjalanan Salib Paroki St. Peter, Kudat telah berlangsung dengan penuh makna di Simpang Mengayau, Kudat, dan dihadiri oleh umat Paroki St. Peter. Peristiwa ini menjadi detik bersejarah kerana buat pertama kalinya Misa Kudus diraikan di Simpang Mengayau — di hujung Borneo, hujung Sabah.

Dalam homilinya, Rev. Fr. Rayner menekankan bahawa Perjalanan Salib ini melambangkan panggilan untuk membawa Salib Kristus ke seluruh pelusuk bumi. Simpang Mengayau, yang terletak di penghujung Sabah, menjadi simbol bahawa tiada tempat yang terlalu jauh untuk menerima khabar sukacita. Begitu juga kita sebagai umat, dipanggil untuk membawa berita keselamatan dan harapan ini ke seluruh dunia melalui kehidupan dan kesaksian kita.

Selepas Misa Kudus, Fr. Rayner bersama seluruh umat berarak menuju ke Tugu Tip of Borneo sambil membawa Salib, sebagai tanda iman yang terus berjalan, bergerak, dan hidup. Perjalanan ini kemudiannya disusuli dengan jamuan makan secara potluck, mempereratkan lagi ikatan persaudaraan sesama umat.

Semoga Perjalanan Salib di perhentian ini menjadi sumber penghiburan, harapan, dan khabar sukacita bagi mereka yang memerlukan, serta menguatkan iman semua umat yang terlibat. ✨✝️

The Way of the Cross  St. Peter’s Parish, Kudat

📍 Simpang Mengayau, Kudat
📅 10 January 2025
✝️ Celebrant: Rev. Fr. Rayner

The Way of the Cross of St. Peter’s Parish, Kudat was prayerfully held at Simpang Mengayau, Kudat, and attended by the parishioners of St. Peter’s Parish. This marked a historic moment as it was the first time a Holy Mass was celebrated at Simpang Mengayau — the northernmost tip of Borneo, the edge of Sabah.

In his homily, Rev. Fr. Rayner reflected on the symbolism of carrying the Cross to the ends of the earth. Simpang Mengayau, standing at the very tip of Sabah, became a powerful sign that no place is too far to receive the Good News. Likewise, we as parishioners are called to carry this message of hope, love, and salvation to every corner of the world through our lives and witness.

After the Holy Mass, Rev. Fr. Rayner and the parishioners processed together with the Cross towards the Tip of Borneo monument, a visible sign of faith that journeys forward and remains alive. The gathering concluded with a potluck fellowship meal, strengthening the spirit of unity and communion among the parishioners.

May this station of the Way of the Cross bring comfort, hope, and the Good News to those in need, and continue to strengthen the faith of all who took part. ✨✝️

Perjalanan Salib Paroki St. Peter, Kudat

📍 Simpang Mengayau, Kudat
📅 10 Januari 2025
✝️ Selebran: Rev. Fr. Rayner

Perjalanan Salib Paroki St. Peter, Kudat telah berlangsung dengan penuh makna di Simpang Mengayau, Kudat, dan dihadiri oleh umat Paroki St. Peter. Peristiwa ini menjadi detik bersejarah kerana buat pertama kalinya Misa Kudus diraikan di Simpang Mengayau — di hujung Borneo, hujung Sabah.

Dalam homilinya, Rev. Fr. Rayner menekankan bahawa Perjalanan Salib ini melambangkan panggilan untuk membawa Salib Kristus ke seluruh pelusuk bumi. Simpang Mengayau, yang terletak di penghujung Sabah, menjadi simbol bahawa tiada tempat yang terlalu jauh untuk menerima khabar sukacita. Begitu juga kita sebagai umat, dipanggil untuk membawa berita keselamatan dan harapan ini ke seluruh dunia melalui kehidupan dan kesaksian kita.

Selepas Misa Kudus, Fr. Rayner bersama seluruh umat berarak menuju ke Tugu Tip of Borneo sambil membawa Salib, sebagai tanda iman yang terus berjalan, bergerak, dan hidup. Perjalanan ini kemudiannya disusuli dengan jamuan makan secara potluck, mempereratkan lagi ikatan persaudaraan sesama umat.

Semoga Perjalanan Salib di perhentian ini menjadi sumber penghiburan, harapan, dan khabar sukacita bagi mereka yang memerlukan, serta menguatkan iman semua umat yang terlibat. ✨✝️

The Way of the Cross  St. Peter’s Parish, Kudat

📍 Simpang Mengayau, Kudat
📅 10 January 2025
✝️ Celebrant: Rev. Fr. Rayner

The Way of the Cross of St. Peter’s Parish, Kudat was prayerfully held at Simpang Mengayau, Kudat, and attended by the parishioners of St. Peter’s Parish. This marked a historic moment as it was the first time a Holy Mass was celebrated at Simpang Mengayau — the northernmost tip of Borneo, the edge of Sabah.

In his homily, Rev. Fr. Rayner reflected on the symbolism of carrying the Cross to the ends of the earth. Simpang Mengayau, standing at the very tip of Sabah, became a powerful sign that no place is too far to receive the Good News. Likewise, we as parishioners are called to carry this message of hope, love, and salvation to every corner of the world through our lives and witness.

After the Holy Mass, Rev. Fr. Rayner and the parishioners processed together with the Cross towards the Tip of Borneo monument, a visible sign of faith that journeys forward and remains alive. The gathering concluded with a potluck fellowship meal, strengthening the spirit of unity and communion among the parishioners.

May this station of the Way of the Cross bring comfort, hope, and the Good News to those in need, and continue to strengthen the faith of all who took part. ✨✝️

開挖軟體torsa後處理程式torsdf.exe說明
torsa軟體由國內大地專業開發完成，其過程和國外軟體rido類似，但採用視窗介面處理，直接在螢幕上輸入各開挖支撐及樓板的位置和勁度，分析產生的結果分為圖形檔和文字檔，其中文字檔分[＊.i]（輸入檔，類似excrido.rid）及[*.o]（輸出檔類似Excan.lst）。
後處理程式之原始碼由主程式torsdf.for+副程式strutf+ridusd+impdat+rifscol組成，其過程和riddf.exe雷同，輸入檔可以選擇直接由[*.i]得到相關輸入參數,亦可由[Excrido.rid]檔得到，而[＊.o]類似rido 的輸出檔[*.lst]；至於後處理過程和[riddf.exe]如出一轍，輸出在torsdf.opt中，也show出分析過程的開挖深度，支撐高程和應力檢核等,然後是壁體深度內之變形和應力包絡線，連續壁配筋，再來是壁體外沉陷量和距離的關係；最後是選取深度內想要輸出步驟之變形，彎矩，剪力和主被動彈簧等作為excel繪圖之用。
照片中有分順打和逆打例，逆打的特色是往下開挖後隨即灌注樓版，至最下開挖才前可能需施作水平支撐。
